10:7.headline: The heads were sent in pots, or in baskets
10:7.body: The seventy heads were sent בדודים. Rashi and Metzudat Zion say in pots, as in I Samuel 2:14. Radak, with the Targum, says in baskets, as in 'two baskets of figs'.

sources.quote: בַּדּוּדִים. סִירוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says the word means pots.

sources.quote: כעין קדירות, וכן (שמואל א ב יד): והכה בכיור או בדוד
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says they were like cooking pots, as in I Samuel 2:14.

sources.quote: בסלים וכן תרגום יונתן בסליא וכמוהו שני דודאי תאנים
sources.says: Radak says it means baskets, as the Targum has it, like 'two baskets of figs'.

10:9.headline: 'You are righteous': praise, or a jab at the crowd
10:9.body: Jehu tells the people צדקים אתם, you are righteous. Rashi and Metzudat David hear a jab: you think you are righteous and I am wicked, but who killed all these? Radak reads it straight: you are not guilty of their blood.

sources.quote: כֻּלְּכֶם בְּעֵינֵיכֶם צַדִּיקִים, וּמַחֲזִיקִים אוֹתִי בְּחֶזְקַת רָשָׁע
sources.says: Rashi says Jehu means that in their own eyes they are righteous and they hold him to be wicked.

sources.quote: הנה תחשבו שאתם צדיקים ממני
sources.says: Metzudat David says Jehu means they think they are more righteous than he is.

sources.quote: אינכם חייבים בדם אלה האנשים
sources.says: Radak says Jehu means they are not guilty of these men's blood.

10:11.headline: Ahab's 'priests' were idol priests, or his close friends
10:11.body: Jehu killed Ahab's כהנים. Metzudat Zion says they were the priests of Baal. Radak says priests of the high places, and notes that the Targum reads 'his friends'.

sources.quote: וכהניו. כהני הבעל
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says they were the priests of Baal.

sources.quote: כהני במות וי"ת וחברוהי
sources.says: Radak says they were priests of the high places, and that the Targum renders 'his friends'.

10:12.headline: Beth-eked: the place where shepherds tied up their sheep
10:12.body: The place name בית עקד comes from tying. Radak, citing his father, says shepherds sheared their flocks there and tied the sheep's legs while shearing. Metzudat Zion links it to 'he bound Isaac'. Rashi says it was where shepherds gathered.

sources.quote: כי נקרא כן לפי שהיו הרועים גוזזים שם את צאנם ובעת הגזיזה קושרים אותם ברגליהם
sources.says: Radak cites his father that it was named for the shepherds who sheared there and tied the sheep by their legs.

sources.quote: קרוי עקד, מלשון (בראשית כב ט): ויעקוד את יצחק
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is called עקד from 'he bound Isaac'.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן קֶשֶׁר, מְקוֹם אֲסֵפַת רוֹעִים
sources.says: Rashi says it means tying, a place where shepherds gather.

10:13.headline: Ahaziah's 'brothers' were really his nephews
10:13.body: The men say they are אחי, brothers, of Ahaziah. Radak says they were his brothers' sons, as Chronicles says, and a nephew can be called a brother, as Lot is called Abraham's brother. Malbim adds that Ahaziah's brothers had already been killed.

sources.quote: ובן אחיו קורא אחיו כמו ואת לוט אחיו
sources.says: Radak says a brother's son is called a brother, as with Lot.

sources.quote: שהיו בני אחי אחזיהו כי אחי אחזיהו נהרגו בגדוד הערבים
sources.says: Malbim says Chronicles shows they were the sons of Ahaziah's brothers, since his brothers were killed by Arab raiders.

10:13.headline: The 'great lady' is Jezebel, who held the real power
10:13.body: The men came to greet the king's sons and the sons of הגבירה, the great lady. Rashi says she is Jezebel. Radak says she is named on her own because the honor rested on her: even in Ahab's lifetime, Ahab did what she said.

sources.quote: וּבְנֵי הַגְּבִירָה. אִיזֶבֶל
sources.says: Rashi says the great lady is Jezebel.

sources.quote: לפי שהכבוד היה תלוי בה שאף בחיי אחאב היתה היא גבירה ואחאב היה נשמע אליה
sources.says: Radak says she is mentioned because the honor depended on her, and Ahab obeyed her even in his life.

10:15.headline: 'It is, it is': both Jehonadab's words, or an answer and reply?
10:15.body: Radak gives two readings of יש ויש. Jehonadab says 'it is' twice to stress it. Or Jehonadab says 'it is', and Jehu answers 'if it is, give me your hand'.

sources.quote: יהונדב אמר יש ויש כפל לחזק
sources.says: Radak first says Jehonadab said it twice for emphasis.

sources.quote: או פירושו ויש תשובת יהוא דרך שאלה
sources.says: Radak then offers that the second ויש is Jehu's reply, as if asking 'if so'.

10:19.headline: Jehu's trick is the word Esau used for Jacob's cheating
10:19.body: בעקבה appears only here. Rashi reads it as deceit, from the same word as Esau's complaint about Jacob, 'he has tricked me twice'. The Targum renders it 'with wisdom'.

sources.quote: בְּמִרְמָה, לְשׁוֹן: וַיַּעְקְבֵנִי
sources.says: Rashi says it means deceit, the same word as 'he tricked me'.

sources.quote: תרגם יונתן: בחוכמא, וכן (בראשית כז לו): ויעקבני זה פעמים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion gives the Targum's 'with wisdom' and compares Genesis 27:36.

10:22.headline: The wardrobe of Baal's priests: a word with its letters swapped
10:22.body: המלתחה appears only here. Rashi, with the Targum, says it held the chests where the garments of Baal's worshippers were wrapped and stored. Metzudat Zion says it is the word for swaddling in Job, חתולה, with its letters turned around.

sources.quote: אַרְגָּזִים וְקֻפְסָאוֹת, שֶׁכּוֹרְכִין בְּתוֹכָן וְגוֹנְזִין תַּכְשִׁיטֵי עוֹבְדֵי הַבַּעַל
sources.says: Rashi says these were chests and boxes where the Baal worshippers' garments were wrapped and stored.

sources.quote: והוא הפוך מן (איוב לח ט): וערפל חתולתו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is a store of wrapped priestly garments, and the word is 'swaddling' from Job 38:9 reversed.

10:25.headline: 'They threw': the bodies out, or themselves in a rush
10:25.body: Rashi, with the Targum, says the runners threw out the bodies of the Baal worshippers. Radak and Metzudat David say 'threw' shows their haste: they all but flung themselves toward the city of Baal's temple.

sources.quote: הִשְׁלִיכוּ חֲלָלִים אֶת עוֹבְדֵי הַבַּעַל
sources.says: Rashi says they threw out the slain Baal worshippers.

sources.quote: הוא על דרך הרחבת הלשון מרוב חפזם ומהירותם
sources.says: Radak says the word is a figure of speech for their great haste.

sources.quote: כאילו השליכו את עצמם ללכת עד העיר המיוחדת לבית הבעל
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is as if they threw themselves to go to the city of Baal's temple.

10:27.headline: A crude word is written, a cleaner one is read aloud
10:27.body: Jehu turned Baal's temple into latrines. The written text has למחראות, a blunt word. The reading tradition says למוצאות instead. Radak says both mean the same, but the word read aloud is cleaner language.

sources.quote: כתיב וקרי למוצאות ושניהם ענין אחד אלא שהקרי לשון נקיה יותר
sources.says: Radak says the written and read words mean the same, but the read word is cleaner.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן בֵּית הַכִּסֵּא
sources.says: Rashi says the word means a latrine.

10:30.headline: Four generations of kings for ending Ahab's four generations
10:30.body: God promises Jehu בני רבעים, sons to the fourth generation, on Israel's throne. Rashi says this was in return for wiping out Ahab's house, which had ruled four generations: Omri, Ahab, Ahaziah and Jehoram.

sources.quote: תַּחַת שֶׁהִשְׁמַדְתָּ אֶת בֵּית אַחְאָב שֶׁמָּלְכוּ אַרְבַּע דּוֹרוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says Jehu gets four generations in return for destroying Ahab's house of four generations.

sources.quote: יהואחז יהואש ירבעם זכריהו
sources.says: Radak names Jehu's four heirs: Jehoahaz, Joash, Jeroboam and Zechariah.

10:32.headline: God began to cut Israel short, or to grow weary of it
10:32.body: Rashi reads לקצות like 'I am weary of my life'. Metzudat Zion reads it as cutting off, as in 'you shall cut off her hand'. Malbim reads it as striking those at Israel's edge, east of the Jordan.

sources.quote: לְקַצּוֹת. כְּמוֹ: קַצְתִּי בְּחַיָּי
sources.says: Rashi compares 'I am weary of my life'.

sources.quote: להכרית, כמו (דברים כה יב): וקצותה את כפה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means to cut off, as in Deuteronomy 25:12.

sources.quote: שהחל להכות היושבים בקצה
sources.says: Malbim says God began to strike those living at the edge of the land.

11:2.headline: The 'bed chamber' where the baby hid may mean the Temple
11:2.body: חדר המטות means 'the room of beds'. Radak first reads it as a room where priests and Levites slept, but Rashi says it was the upper room of the Holy of Holies, named after the verse 'he lies between my breasts'.

sources.quote: וְקוֹרֵא אוֹתָהּ חֲדַר הַמִּטּוֹת, עַל שֵׁם: בֵּין שָׁדַי יָלִין
sources.says: Rashi says the hiding place was the upper room of the Holy of Holies, called the bed chamber after the phrase 'between my breasts he lies'.

sources.quote: בחדר המטות החדר שהיה בעזרת הלוים או הכהנים
sources.says: Radak explains it as a room in the court of the Levites or priests, and then brings the teaching that the Temple is called the bed chamber.

11:4.headline: The captains are called כרי, a word that also means rams
11:4.body: Rashi says כרי is a group name for the king's mighty men. Metzudat Zion says it is the same as כרים, rams, used as a borrowed name for officers, and points to 'the blood of rams' in Isaiah 34:6.

sources.quote: וּלְשׁוֹן כָּרִי שֶׁלֹּא אָמַר לַכָּרִים, שֵׁם דָּבָר שֶל קְבוּצַת הַגִּבּוֹרִים
sources.says: Rashi says כרי, not כרים, is a collective name for the band of mighty men.

sources.quote: כמו לכרים, ויקראו כן השרים, על דרך השאלה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means כרים and the officers are called that by a borrowed image, as in 'the blood of rams' in Isaiah.

11:6.headline: The Gate of Sur is named for turning away the impure
11:6.body: סור means 'turn aside'. The sages say this east gate got its name because impure people turned away there, as in 'Turn aside, unclean!' in Lamentations 4:15.

sources.quote: שער סור ששם היו טמאים פורשים הה"ד סורו טמא קראו למו
sources.says: Radak brings the sages' view that it is the east gate, called Sur because the impure turned away from there.

sources.quote: ויקרא כן על שם שמשם היו הטמאים פורשים
sources.says: Metzudat David says the gate is called this because the impure separated there, after 'Turn aside, unclean'.

11:6.headline: An odd word read as 'never let your attention slip'
11:6.body: Rashi reads מסח as coming from letting your mind drift, so the order is 'guard it closely'. Radak gives that reading too, and another from נסח, 'tear down', meaning do not break your ranks.

sources.quote: שִׁמְרוּהוּ מְאֹד, שֶׁלֹּא תַסִּיחוּ דַעְתְּכֶם
sources.says: Rashi says it means guard it closely and do not let your mind wander.

sources.quote: שתשמרו ממסח והיא הנתיצה וההריסה כמו ונסחתם מעל האדמה
sources.says: Radak first reads it as guarding against a breaking down of the guard line, from the root of 'you will be torn off the land', and then offers the 'do not let your mind wander' reading.

11:12.headline: The 'testimony' given the boy king: a Torah scroll, or the crown?
11:12.body: Rashi says העדות, 'the testimony', is a Torah scroll, or, as the sages say, the crown itself, which fit only a rightful heir. Radak also reads it as royal finery, from עדי, 'jewelry'.

sources.quote: הַנֵּזֶר הוּא הָעֵדוּת, שֶׁכָּל הָרָאוּי לַמַּלְכוּת הוֹלַמְתּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it is a Torah scroll, and brings the sages' view that the crown was the testimony because it fit only one fit to rule.

sources.quote: בגדי מלכות מן ועדית עדי
sources.says: Radak says it means royal garments, from the word for ornament.

11:13.headline: The 'runners' may be people dancing for joy
11:13.body: הרצין ends with an unusual nun where a mem is expected. Radak says it is the sound of celebration, and the Aramaic translation reads it as people dancing.

sources.quote: ונו"ן הרצין במקום מ"ם
sources.says: Radak says the nun stands for a mem, and the sound was the joy of people shouting 'long live the king', dancing and clapping.

sources.quote: יַת קַל דְרַקְדָנִין עַמָא
sources.says: The Aramaic translation renders it 'the sound of the people dancing'.

11:18.headline: Mattan: a priest's name, or 'those given' to the priest?
11:18.body: Radak says מתן was the name of the priest of Baal. Ralbag thinks it means those given over to the priest, the other priests who served with him, and all of them were killed.

sources.quote: כהן הבעל היה שמו מתן
sources.says: Radak says the priest of Baal was named Mattan.

sources.quote: אחשוב שהרצון בזה שהנתנים לכהן לבעל
sources.says: Ralbag suggests it means the priests given to serve with the priest of Baal, and they were all killed before the altars.

12:3.headline: 'All his days': not his whole life, only while Jehoiada lived
12:3.body: The verse seems to say Joash did right all his life. Radak says it means only the days Jehoiada taught him, since he turned bad after Jehoiada died. Rashi cites a midrash: the princes then flattered Joash as a god, because he had hidden in the Holy of Holies for six years.

sources.quote: לא כל ימיו כי אחרי מות יהוידע עשה הרע בעיני ה' כמו שכתוב בדברי הימים אלא פי' כל הימים אשר הורהו יהוידע הכהן
sources.says: Radak says it is not all his days, since after Jehoiada died he did evil, but all the days Jehoiada the priest taught him.

sources.quote: הַנִּכְנָס לְבֵית קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים שָׁעָה אַחַת מְסֻכָּן לָמוּת, וְאַתָּה נֶחְבֵּאתָ בּוֹ שֵׁשׁ שָׁנִים, כְּדַאי אַתָּה לִהְיוֹת אֱלוֹהַּ
sources.says: Rashi says the princes told Joash: one who enters the Holy of Holies for an hour risks death, and you hid there six years, so you deserve to be a god.

12:4.headline: These 'high places' were altars to God, not idols
12:4.body: The verse faults the people for the high places. Metzudat David says these were private altars to God. They were forbidden once the Temple was built.

sources.quote: במות יחיד לשמים, ואסור הוא משנבנה הבית
sources.says: Metzudat David says they were private altars for the sake of Heaven, forbidden since the Temple was built.

12:5.headline: 'Passing money': the yearly half-shekel, or loose gifts?
12:5.body: Rashi, Radak and Metzudat David say 'money that passes' is the yearly half-shekel. It is named for the Torah's words 'everyone who passes among those counted'. Ralbag says it means money with no fixed yearly amount, like vows and gifts.

sources.quote: כֶּסֶף עוֹבֵר, הוּא כֶּסֶף הַשְּׁקָלִים שֶׁבְּכָל שָׁנָה, הַנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ: כָּל הָעוֹבֵר עַל הַפְּקֻדִים
sources.says: Rashi says 'passing money' is the yearly shekel money, about which it says 'everyone who passes among those counted'.

sources.quote: הוא הכסף שאינו מוגבל בכל שנה ושנ' כמו ההקדשות והערכין
sources.says: Ralbag says it is money not fixed each year, like dedications and valuations.

12:6.headline: A 'breach' is named for the checking it needs
12:6.body: בדק means a crack or break in the building. Radak and Metzudat Zion link it to בדק, 'to check'. A break is called this because someone must inspect it to see what it needs.

sources.quote: בדק הבית מקום השבר וההריסה ונקרא בדק לפי שצריך לבדקו ולעמוד עליו מה יצטרך
sources.says: Radak says the breach is the place of damage, called בדק because it must be inspected to see what it needs.

sources.quote: מקום השבר והרעוע, יקרא בדק, כי מהצורך לבדוק ולחפש אחריו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says a broken or shaky spot is called בדק because it needs checking and searching.

12:9.headline: The priests 'agreed', glad to be free of suspicion
12:9.body: ויאתו is a rare word for 'they agreed', as in Genesis 'on this we will agree'. Radak says the priests were glad to take no money at all, so no one would suspect them.

sources.quote: ויאותו. נתרצו, כמו (בראשית לד טו): בזאת נאות לכם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means they consented, as in 'on this condition we will agree with you'.

sources.quote: וישר בעיניהם שלא יקחוהו כלל כדי שלא יהיו נחשדים בזה הדבר
sources.says: Radak says it pleased them not to take the money at all, so they would not be suspected.

12:10.headline: 'Keepers of the threshold': doorkeepers, or keepers of the vessels?
12:10.body: סף usually means a threshold. Rashi says these men held the keys to the courtyard gates, seven of them for seven gates. Radak and Ralbag say סף is a general name for Temple vessels, so they guarded the vessels.

sources.quote: סִפֵּי הָעֲזָרָה, הַמְמֻנִּים עַל מַפְתְּחוֹת הָעֲזָרָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means the thresholds of the courtyard, the men in charge of the courtyard keys.

sources.quote: שומרי כלי הבית וסף הוא שם כלל לכלי השרת
sources.says: Radak says they guarded the Temple vessels, since סף is a general name for the service vessels.

12:11.headline: They 'bound up' the silver, or minted it into coins?
12:11.body: ויצרו can come from צרור, a bundle, or from צורה, a form. Ralbag and Radak say they tied the silver in bags. Metzudat David says they struck it into coins to pay the workers.

sources.quote: היו משימים את הכסף בצרורות והיו מונים
sources.says: Ralbag says they put the silver into bags and counted it.

sources.quote: עשו בהם צורת מטבע, להוציאם, בהוצאה
sources.says: Metzudat David says they gave the silver the form of coins to spend it.

sources.quote: ויש לפרש ויצורו מענין צורה כי הכסף שלא היה מטבע עשו אותו מטבע
sources.says: Radak says it can also be read from 'form': silver that was not coin they made into coin.

12:14.headline: Silver 'basins': jugs, cups for blood, or musical instruments?
12:14.body: ספות is a rare word for a vessel. Metzudat Zion says they were shaped like jugs, like Rebekah's water jug. Ralbag says they held blood or wine for offerings. Rashi groups them with the music instruments.

sources.quote: שם כלים עשוים כצורת כדים, כי תרגם יונתן: קולין
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says they were vessels shaped like jugs, as the Targum renders them.

sources.quote: הם כלים לקבל הדם או יין הנסכים
sources.says: Ralbag says they were vessels to receive blood or libation wine.

sources.quote: סִפּוֹת כֶּסֶף מְזַמְּרוֹת. וְהֵם כְּלֵי שִׁיר
sources.says: Rashi says the silver ספות and מזמרות were musical instruments.

12:16.headline: No audit for honest men: the source of a charity rule
12:16.body: The verse says no one checked the accounts of the men who paid the workers. Radak says the Sages learned from this that charity collectors are not audited. Ralbag says people are careful around holy money.

sources.quote: מכאן ארז"ל שאין מחשבין עם גבאי צדקה
sources.says: Radak says from here the Sages learned that charity collectors are not made to give an accounting.

sources.quote: כי הקדש מבדל בדילי אינשי מיניה
sources.says: Ralbag says people keep their distance from holy property.

12:17.headline: Leftover guilt-offering money: Jehoiada's clever reading
12:17.body: Money set aside for a sin or guilt offering sometimes had some left over. Rashi and Radak cite Jehoiada's reading: one verse says a guilt offering is 'for God', another 'for the priest'. So the leftover bought burnt offerings: the meat to God, the hides to the priests.

sources.quote: אמרו זה מדרש דרש יהוידע הכהן אשם הוא לה' אשם הוא לכהן
sources.says: Radak says the Sages call this a reading of Jehoiada the priest: a guilt offering is for God, and a guilt offering is for the priest.

sources.quote: וְהֵם לוֹקְחִים מֵהֶם עוֹלוֹת קַיִץ לַמִּזְבֵּחַ, הַבָּשָׂר לְעוֹלָה, וְהָעוֹרוֹת שֶׁלָּהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says the priests bought burnt offerings with it for the altar, the meat for the offering and the hides for themselves.

12:18.headline: 'Then' Hazael attacked: after Joash turned bad
12:18.body: The verse does not say when 'then' was. Rashi says it was after Jehoiada died and Joash let himself be made a god. Radak says it was when Joash began doing evil.

sources.quote: אַחַר מוֹת יְהוֹיָדָע, וְעָשָׂה יוֹאָשׁ אֶת עַצְמוֹ אֱלוֹהַּ
sources.says: Rashi says it was after Jehoiada died and Joash made himself a god.

sources.quote: פירוש כשעשה הרע בעיני ה' אחרי מות יהוידע והביא עליהם האל מלך ארם
sources.says: Radak says it means when Joash did evil after Jehoiada's death, and God brought the king of Aram on them.

12:22.headline: Killed by sons of an Ammonite and a Moabite mother
12:22.body: Chronicles names the killers' mothers as an Ammonite and a Moabite. Rashi and Radak say this is a lesson. Ammon and Moab repaid Abraham's kindness with ingratitude. So their sons punished Joash, who repaid Jehoiada's kindness by killing his son.

sources.quote: לְלַמֵּד שֶׁנִּפְרַע מִמֶּנּוּ הַקָּבָּ"ה עַל יְדֵי אֲנָשִׁים כַּיּוֹצֵא בוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it teaches that God punished Joash through people like himself.

sources.quote: יבואו עמונית ומואבית כפויי טובה שכפו בטובתו של אברהם אבינו
sources.says: Radak says: let the ungrateful Ammonite and Moabite come, who denied the kindness of Abraham our father.

17:3.headline: וישב: Hoshea "paid back" tribute, not just paid it
17:3.body: וישב means "returned". Malbim asks why the verse does not just say "gave". He says Hoshea paid back the tribute for the years he had held it back. Metzudat David says it was a yearly tax, given again and again.

sources.quote: מהו לשון וישב לו מנחה היה לו לומר ויתן לו, לא לשון השבה
sources.says: Malbim asks why it says "returned tribute" and not simply "gave".

sources.quote: שלא נתן כל ימי מרידתו השיב בעד שנים שעברו
sources.says: Malbim says that what Hoshea had not paid during his revolt, he paid back for the past years.

sources.quote: לפי שהיה קבוע עליו לכל שנה אמר ׳וישב׳, כי נתן וחזר ונתן
sources.says: Metzudat David says it was fixed for every year, so it says "returned": he gave and gave again.

17:6.headline: ויגל with a segol: the king of Assyria exiled Israel
17:6.body: The same letters, ויגל, can mean "went into exile" or "sent into exile". Rashi says the vowel decides. Here, with a segol, the king of Assyria exiled Israel. In verse 23, with a hiriq, Israel went into exile.

sources.quote: וַיֶּגֶל אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל. וַיַּגְלֶה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
sources.says: Rashi says ויגל here means "and he exiled Israel".

sources.quote: וְאִם הוּא מְדַבֵּר בִּלְשׁוֹן מַפְעִיל
sources.says: Rashi explains that when the verb means causing someone else to act, the first letter takes a segol.

17:12.headline: גלולים: idols called by a word for dung
17:12.body: Metzudat Zion says this word for idols comes from גלל, dung. Malbim says these were images of loathsome beasts, served on purpose to anger God.

sources.quote: הגלולים. מלשון גלל וצואה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says גלולים comes from the words for dung and filth.

sources.quote: והוסיפו יותר שעבדו גלולים שהוא דמות חיות ובהמות המגועלים
sources.says: Malbim says they went further and served גלולים, images of loathsome animals.

17:13.headline: Written "His prophet", read "the prophets of"
17:13.body: The written text has נביאו, "His prophet", and it is read נביאי. Radak says the written form means only God's true prophets, not false ones. He adds a midrash: God sent prophet after prophet, one in the morning and one in the evening.

sources.quote: ביד כל מי שהיה נביאו לא נביאי השקר
sources.says: Radak says the written form means by everyone who was His prophet, not the false prophets.

sources.quote: ובדרש ביד כל נביאו כמה נביאים העידותי בהם אחד בשחרית ואחד בין הערבים
sources.says: Radak cites a midrash: how many prophets I sent to warn them, one in the morning and one in the evening.

17:13.headline: נביא and חוזה: why the verse names both kinds of prophet
17:13.body: Metzudat David says נביא was used even for prophets of Baal, but חוזה, a seer, only for God's prophets. Ralbag says a חוזה is higher: a נביא may hear God in a dream, while a חוזה sees a vision.

sources.quote: כי שם נביא משותף הוא גם לנביאי הבעל, מה שאין כן חוזה, כי הוא בלתי לה׳ לבדו
sources.says: Metzudat David says the name נביא is shared with the prophets of Baal, but חוזה is used only for God's.

sources.quote: וידמה שהחוזה הוא יותר שלם מהנבי' כי הנביא יקרא נביא אפילו בא אליו דבר ה' בחלום
sources.says: Ralbag says a חוזה seems more complete than a נביא, since one is called נביא even if God's word came in a dream.

sources.quote: ואולם החוזה יקרא אשר יבא אליו דבר ה' במראה והוא למעלה מהחלו'
sources.says: Ralbag says a חוזה receives God's word in a vision, which is above a dream.

17:15.headline: They followed הבל, emptiness, and became empty
17:15.body: The verse uses one root twice. They went after הבל, "vapor, emptiness", and ויהבלו, became empty themselves. Metzudat David says they became devoted to idols. Ralbag says their own deeds became empty.

sources.quote: נעשו בעלי הבל, ואדוקים לעבודת גלולים
sources.says: Metzudat David says they became people of emptiness, devoted to idol worship.

sources.quote: ועשו גם כן פעולותיהם הבלים
sources.says: Ralbag says they followed emptiness, that is idolatry, and made their own deeds empty too.

17:21.headline: Written "threw", read "drove away": Jeroboam cast Israel off
17:21.body: The written word is וידא, and it is read וידח. Ralbag says the written form means "threw", as in casting lots, and the read form "drove away". Both say Jeroboam cast Israel away from God. Radak reads the written form as "pushed far off".

sources.quote: וידא כתוב וידח קרי והכתי' הוא מענין ידו גורל והרצון בו וישליך
sources.says: Ralbag says it is written וידא and read וידח, and the written form is from "they cast lots", meaning he threw.

sources.quote: וכן כונת הקרי מסכמת לזה הענין כי ההדחה מתיחסת מאד אל ההשלכה
sources.says: Ralbag says the read form agrees, since driving away is close to throwing away.

sources.quote: והכתוב פי' מן המנדים ליום רע שונאיכם מנדיכם ופי' הרחיק מאחרי ה' את ישראל
sources.says: Radak says the written form is from a word for casting out, meaning he pushed Israel far from God.

17:23.headline: ויגל with a hiriq: Israel went into exile
17:23.body: These are the same letters as in verse 6. Rashi says the hiriq vowel here means Israel went into exile, not that someone exiled them.

sources.quote: שֶׁהוּא לְשׁוֹן גָּלָה, וְאֵינוֹ לְשׁוֹן הִגְלָה
sources.says: Rashi says this is pointed with a hiriq, meaning "went into exile", not "sent into exile".

17:29.headline: The "Shomronim" here are Israelites, not the newcomers
17:29.body: This word appears only here. Rashi, Radak and Metzudat David say it means the Israelites who had lived in Samaria. The new peoples set their idols in the shrines Israel had built.

sources.quote: אֲשֶׁר עָשׂוּ הַשֹּׁמְרֹנִים. יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּעוֹדָם שָׁם
sources.says: Rashi says the Shomronim are Israel, while they still lived there.

sources.quote: זה ישראל שהיו בשמרון ובאותם בתי הבמות שעשו הם הניחו אלו הגוים אלהיהם
sources.says: Radak says this means Israel who lived in Samaria, and the new peoples placed their gods in the shrines Israel had made.

sources.quote: השמרנים. היהודים, אנשי שומרון עד לא גלו
sources.says: Metzudat David says they are the Jews, the people of Samaria before they were exiled.

17:30.headline: סכות בנות: an idol shaped like a hen with her chicks
17:30.body: Rashi says this Babylonian idol was a hen with her chicks. Radak explains the name: סכות is like סכוי, a word for a rooster, and בנות, "daughters", are the chicks.

sources.quote: דְּמוּת תַּרְנְגֹלֶת עִם אֶפְרוֹחֶיהָ
sources.says: Rashi says it was the image of a hen with her chicks.

sources.quote: וכמו שקורין לתרנגול סכוי כן היו קורין לתרנגול סכות ובנות פי' עם אפרוחיה
sources.says: Radak says that as a rooster is called סכוי, it was called סכות, and בנות means with her chicks.

17:30.headline: אשימא: a goat idol, named for its bare hide
17:30.body: Rashi says it was shaped like a goat. Radak says it was a bald goat, called אשימא because it has no wool, like שומם, "desolate". He also cites a reading of it as a lamb, from איל האשם, the guilt-offering ram.

sources.quote: אֲשִׁימָא. דְּמוּת תַּיִשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says Ashima was the image of a goat.

sources.quote: ונקרא אשימא לפי שאין לו צמר והוא כמו שומם
sources.says: Radak says it is called Ashima because it has no wool, as in שומם, desolate.

sources.quote: ובירושלמי אשימא. אימרא כמה דתימא באיל האשם
sources.says: Radak cites the Jerusalem Talmud: Ashima is a lamb, as in "the guilt-offering ram".

17:31.headline: נבחז: a dog idol, named "barks and shows"
17:31.body: Rashi says it was shaped like a dog. Radak says the name joins two words: נובח, "barks", and חז, "shows", for a dog that bares its teeth.

sources.quote: נִבְחַז. דְּמוּת כֶּלֶב
sources.says: Rashi says Nibhaz was the image of a dog.

sources.quote: ופי' נבחז הוא כלב והיא מלה מורכבת נובח חז נובח מן לא יוכלו לנבוח חז לשון מראה שמראה שיניו
sources.says: Radak says Nibhaz is a dog, a word made of נובח, barking, and חז, showing, because it shows its teeth.

17:31.headline: אדרמלך: a mule idol, "it carries for its master"
17:31.body: Rashi says it was shaped like a mule. Radak explains the name: the mule carries all its master's loads.

sources.quote: לְאַדְרַמֶּלֶךְ. דְּמוּת פֶּרֶד
sources.says: Rashi says Adrammelech was the image of a mule.

sources.quote: אדרמלך הוא הפרד ונקרא כן דאדר ליה למריה בטועניה פי' שנושא לרבו כל משאותיו
sources.says: Radak says Adrammelech is the mule, named because it carries all its master's burdens.

17:31.headline: ענמלך: a horse idol, "it answers its master in battle"
17:31.body: Rashi says it was shaped like a horse. Radak explains the name: the horse answers its master in battle.

sources.quote: וַעֲנַמֶּלֶךְ. דְּמוּת סוּס
sources.says: Rashi says Anammelech was the image of a horse.

sources.quote: ענמלך זה הסוס דעני ליה למריה בקרבא
sources.says: Radak says Anammelech is the horse, which answers its master in battle.

17:34.headline: They "feared" God only because of the lions
17:34.body: Verse 33 says these peoples feared God, and verse 34 says they did not. Rashi says their fear was not whole: they converted out of fear of the lions. Radak adds that they were called "lion converts".

sources.quote: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּתְגַּיְּרוּ מִיִּרְאַת הָאֲרָיוֹת, אֵין יִרְאָתָם אֶת ה' יִרְאָה שְׁלֵמָה
sources.says: Rashi says that though they converted out of fear of the lions, their fear of God was not complete.

sources.quote: לא היו יראים את ה' בלב שלם כי אם מפחד האריות לפיכך קראו אותם גרי אריות
sources.says: Radak says they did not fear God wholeheartedly, only from fear of the lions, so they were called lion converts.

17:34.headline: The name Israel itself argues against serving other powers
17:34.body: Metzudat David says Jacob was named Israel because he strove with a heavenly being and won. So his children should not serve heavenly powers. Radak notes that Jacob got the name just after telling his family to put away foreign gods.

sources.quote: הלא השם הזה היה על שם כי שרה עם האלהים וגו׳ ויוכל, ומזה נראה שאין לעבוד לשרי מעלה
sources.says: Metzudat David says the name comes from "you strove with God and prevailed", which shows one should not serve heavenly powers.

sources.quote: כי אז כשאמר יעקב לבניו הסירו את אלהי הנכר אשר בתוככם והטהרו והחליפו שמלותיכם אז נראה אליו ה' ואמר לו ישראל יהיה שמך
sources.says: Radak says that when Jacob told his sons to remove the foreign gods, God then appeared to him and named him Israel.

18:4.headline: Nechushtan: 'just a piece of copper', a name meant to belittle
18:4.body: Rashi says Hezekiah named Moses' bronze snake to mock it: it is nothing but copper, and the Metzudat David says the added נ makes it smaller. Ralbag hears 'their copper', and Targum Jonathan says it was the worshipers who called it this.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן בִּזָּיוֹן, כְּלוֹמַר מַה צֹּרֶךְ בָּזֶה, אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא נְחַשׁ נְחשֶׁת
sources.says: Rashi says the name is a term of contempt: it is only a copper snake.

sources.quote: ולהקטין מעלתו הוסיף הנו״ן
sources.says: The Metzudat David says the extra נ was added to lower its standing.

sources.quote: והנה קרא לו חזקיה נחשת שלהן
sources.says: Ralbag says Hezekiah called it 'their copper', as if to say it has no power beyond that of copper.

sources.quote: וַהֲווֹ קָרָן לֵיהּ נְחוּשְׁתָּן
sources.says: Targum Jonathan says the people of Israel were the ones who called it Nechushtan.

18:7.headline: 'He acted wisely' here means he succeeded
18:7.body: ישכיל comes from שכל, good sense, but Rashi and Radak say here it means he succeeded. The Metzudat David explains why: a man who succeeds looks to people as if he acts wisely.

sources.quote: יַשְׂכִּיל. יַצְלִיחַ
sources.says: Rashi says ישכיל means he would succeed.

sources.quote: כי המצליח נראה הוא להבריות כאילו עושה מעשיו בהשכל
sources.says: The Metzudat David says one who succeeds looks to people as if he does things with wisdom.

18:10.headline: 'After three years', or from the start of the third?
18:10.body: Radak counts only two years between the start of the siege and the fall of Samaria, so he reads מקצה as 'from the start of the third year'. Targum Jonathan reads it as 'at the end of three years'.

sources.quote: אין כאן כי אם שתי שנים והוא מקצה שלש
sources.says: Radak says only two years passed, so מקצה here means from the start of the third year.

sources.quote: מִסוֹף תְּלַת שְׁנִין
sources.says: Targum Jonathan renders it 'at the end of three years'.

18:18.headline: The 'reminder': who orders the king's cases, or who keeps records?
18:18.body: המזכיר comes from זכר, to remember. Rashi says he reminded the king which case came first so he would judge it first, while the Metzudat David says he was in charge of the book of records.

sources.quote: אֵיזֶה מִשְׁפָּט בָּא לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ רִאשׁוֹן, שֶׁיִּפְסְקֶנּוּ רִאשׁוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says the מזכיר told the king which case came before him first, so he would decide it first.

sources.quote: הממונה על ספר הזכרונות
sources.says: The Metzudat David says he was the official in charge of the book of records.

18:20.headline: 'Mere words of the lips': empty boasting, or prayer?
18:20.body: Radak, following his father, says Rabshakeh mocks Hezekiah for trusting prayer, mere words, when war needs plans and strength. Rashi reads it as Hezekiah's refusal to serve Assyria, which was only talk until the army came.

sources.quote: חשבת להנצל בדבר שפתים כלומר בתפלה
sources.says: Radak gives his father's reading: you thought to be saved by words of the lips, meaning prayer.

sources.quote: אַךְ דְּבַר שְׂפָתַיִם הָיָה, כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא יֵצֵא מִמְּקוֹמוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says Hezekiah's refusal to serve Assyria was only words as long as the king had not come against him.

18:25.headline: 'And destroy it': Rabshakeh's own addition to God's word
18:25.body: Rabshakeh claims God told him to go up against the land and destroy it. Rashi says he added 'destroy it' himself, and the Metzudat David says he took a prophecy about Samaria and wrongly applied it to Jerusalem.

sources.quote: וְהַשְׁחִיתָהּ. אֶת זוֹ הוֹסִיף מִשֶּׁלּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says Rabshakeh added the words 'and destroy it' on his own.

sources.quote: וטעה לומר שכן יעשה לירושלים
sources.says: The Metzudat David says Isaiah's prophecy was about Samaria, and Rabshakeh wrongly said the same would happen to Jerusalem.

18:27.headline: Written crudely, read politely: a coarse word swapped when read aloud
18:27.body: Rabshakeh's coarse word is written in the text, but readers say צואתם, a cleaner word, in its place. Radak says both mean the same, and Maimonides says Hebrew keeps no plain names for such things at all.

sources.quote: חריהם. כן כתיב וקרי צואתם וענין אחד הוא והקרי הוא לשון נקיה
sources.says: Radak says the written word and the word read aloud mean the same, and the one read aloud is clean speech.

sources.quote: וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ פֵּרְשׁוּ: לְכַנּוֹתָם לָשׁוֹן נָאָה צוֹאָתָם
sources.says: Rashi says the Sages explained that it is read צואתם to call it by a nicer word.

sources.quote: לכל הדברים האלה לא נקבעה כלל הוראה ראשונית בלשון העברית
sources.says: Maimonides says Hebrew has no plain words of its own for bodily waste or sex, and uses polite substitutes like צואה and מימי רגלים.

18:27.headline: A coarse word for urine, read aloud as 'water of the feet'
18:27.body: The written word is replaced in reading by מימי רגליהם, 'the water of their feet'. The Metzudat Zion says the written word means urine and is close to שתן, and Radak says it hints at the body's lower parts.

sources.quote: שיניהם. הוא מי רגלים, והוא קרוב מלשון שתן
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says the word means urine and is close to the word שתן.

sources.quote: שניהם. כן כתיב וקרי מימי רגליהם והכתוב הוא רמז לתחתוניות
sources.says: Radak says it is written שניהם and read מימי רגליהם, and the written word hints at the lower parts of the body.

18:32.headline: Why promise only 'a land like yours', not a better one?
18:32.body: Rabshakeh came to tempt the people, so he should have promised a better land. Rashi says he knew they would see through that lie.

sources.quote: הָיָה לוֹ לוֹמַר אֶל אֶרֶץ טוֹבָה מִשֶּׁלָּכֶם, שֶׁהֲרֵי לְפַתּוֹתָם בָּא, אֶלָּא שֶׁיָּדַע שֶׁיַּכִּירוּ שֶׁדְּבָרָיו שֶׁקֶר
sources.says: Rashi says he should have promised a land better than theirs, since he came to tempt them, but he knew they would recognize the lie.

18:34.headline: Hena and Ivvah: two cities, or 'he uprooted and twisted them'?
18:34.body: Ralbag says הנע ועוה are names of cities. Targum Jonathan and the Metzudat David read them as verbs: Assyria moved those peoples from their places and twisted them.

sources.quote: חמת ארפד ספרוים הנע ועוה. הם שמות מדינות
sources.says: Ralbag says these are names of countries.

sources.quote: שמות מדינות או שמות אלהים אחרים ולדעת יונתן פירושו הניע ועוה אותם מארצם
sources.says: Radak says they are names of places or of idols, while Targum Jonathan reads them as 'he moved them and twisted them out of their land'.

sources.quote: הניעם ממקומם והעקימם
sources.says: The Metzudat David says it means he moved them from their place and bent them.

19:3.headline: A city stuck like a mother in labor with no strength left
19:3.body: משבר is the birthing seat, or the opening the baby comes through. Hezekiah says the crisis has reached the moment of birth, but there is no strength to deliver.

sources.quote: עַד צָרָה הַדּוֹמָה לְאִשָּׁה יוֹשֶׁבֶת עַל מַשְׁבֵּר וְאֵין בָּהּ כֹּחַ לֵילֵד
sources.says: Rashi says the trouble is like a woman on the birthing seat with no strength to give birth.

sources.quote: משבר. הוא מקום מושב היולדות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says משבר is the seat where women give birth.

sources.quote: ובא הבן עד המשבר והוא הרחם מקום יציאת הולד
sources.says: Radak says משבר is the womb, the place the child comes out.

19:4.headline: Who argues here: the Assyrian boaster, or God answering him?
19:4.body: והוכיח can mean the Assyrian officer argued his case with insults. It can also mean God will rebuke him for the words He heard.

sources.quote: רבשקה הוכיח בדברי גידופים או פירושו האל יוכיח בדברים אשר שמע
sources.says: Radak gives both readings: Rabshakeh argued with blasphemies, or God will rebuke him for what He heard.

sources.quote: וְיַעֲבֵּיד פּוּרְעֲנוּתָא עַל כָּל פִּתְגָמַיָא
sources.says: The Aramaic translation takes the second reading: God will punish him for all the words.

19:13.headline: City names, or what Assyria did to those cities?
19:13.body: הנע ועוה look like two more town names in the list. The Aramaic translation reads them as verbs: the king of Assyria shook them loose and sent them into exile.

sources.quote: הָא טַלְטִילוּנוּן וְאַגְלִיאוּנוּן
sources.says: The Aramaic translation renders the words as 'they uprooted them and exiled them'.

sources.quote: הֵנַע וְעִוָּה. אוֹתָן מֶלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר
sources.says: Rashi reads the two words as things the king of Assyria did to those places.

19:21.headline: Zion is a 'maiden' because no one has ever conquered her
19:21.body: בתולת, 'maiden', is a picture. A city called a maiden has never been taken by an enemy.

sources.quote: ופירוש בתולת כבתולה שלא נכבשה וכן בכל מקום שזוכר בתולה על עם ועל עדה זהו עניינו
sources.says: Radak says 'maiden' means a city not conquered, and that this is the meaning whenever a people is called a maiden.

sources.quote: וקראה בתולה, על כי לא נכבשה עדיין מעולם
sources.says: Metzudat David says she is called a maiden because she has never yet been conquered.

19:23.headline: 'Lebanon' is the Temple, the place that makes sins white
19:23.body: לבנון sounds like לבן, white. Rashi reads 'the far reaches of Lebanon' as the Temple, because it whitens sins.

sources.quote: יַרְכְּתֵי לְבָנוֹן. בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, שֶׁמַּלְבִּין עֲוֹנוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says Lebanon here means the Temple, which makes sins white.

19:23.headline: Kings says 'lodging', Isaiah says 'height': two homes of God
19:23.body: Sennacherib boasts he will reach מלון קצו, the 'farthest lodging'. Isaiah's copy of this speech says מרום, 'height'. The sages read both: he meant to destroy God's home below and then the one above.

sources.quote: ובדברי רז"ל כתיב מלון קצו וכתיב מרום קצו אמר אותו רשע בתחלה אחריב דירה של מטה ואח"כ אחריב דירה של מעלה
sources.says: Radak quotes the sages: one book says 'lodging' and the other 'height', because the wicked king planned to destroy the lower dwelling first and then the upper one.

sources.quote: מלון קצו. הוא בית המקדש, שהוא מלון ומשכן השכינה
sources.says: Metzudat David says the 'lodging' is the Temple, where God's presence lodges.

19:24.headline: The king boasts he dug down to the spring itself
19:24.body: קרתי, a rare verb, means digging until you reach the source. Its root is the same as in 'ravens will peck it out' in Proverbs.

sources.quote: קרתי. חפרתי אחר מקור, והוא מלשון (משלי ל יז): יקרוה עורבי נחל, שהוא ענין נקב ובקוע
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means 'I dug for a spring', from the Proverbs word for pecking a hole.

sources.quote: אני קרתי.  באתי עד המקור
sources.says: Radak says it means 'I reached the source'.

19:24.headline: 'Strange' waters, or rushing waters?
19:24.body: זרים usually means foreign. Rashi says these are spring waters no one knew before. Metzudat Zion links the word to זרם, a rushing flow.

sources.quote: מַיִם נוֹבְעִים קוֹרֵא זָרִים, לְפִי שֶׁעַד הֵנָּה לֹא הִכִּירוּ בָּהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says spring water is called 'strange' because until then no one knew of it.

sources.quote: זרים. שוטפים, כמו (חבקוק ג י): זרם מים עבר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means flowing, like 'a stream of water' in Habakkuk.

19:25.headline: Heaps sprouting weeds, or heaps laid waste?
19:25.body: נצים can mean blossoms: the walled cities become mounds where plants grow. Radak instead reads it as 'ruined', from a word Jeremiah uses for wasted cities.

sources.quote: נצים. פרחים, כמו (שיר השירים ז יג): הנצו הרמונים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means flowers, as in 'the pomegranates have blossomed'.

sources.quote: לִהְיוֹת לְגַלִּים נִצִּים, לְגַלֵּי אֲדָמָה שֶׁצּוֹמְחִין בָּהֶן יְרָקוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says the cities become mounds of earth where greens grow.

sources.quote: ופי' נצים חרבים מן עריך תצינה
sources.says: Radak says the word means ruined, from 'your cities will be laid waste'.

19:26.headline: Grain struck by blight before it can stand tall
19:26.body: שדפה is the blight that withers grain early. Isaiah's copy spells it with מ instead of פ. Radak says the two letters are made in the same place in the mouth.

sources.quote: ושדפה. מלשון (מלכים א ח ל): שדפון ירקון, והוא לקות הזרע
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word comes from שדפון, a disease of the crop.

sources.quote: ובישעיה ושדמה במ"ם והוא כמו בפ"א כי המ"ם והפ"א ממוצא אחד
sources.says: Radak says Isaiah writes it with a mem, which means the same, since mem and peh come from the same place in the mouth.

19:27.headline: Your 'sitting' means your sitting in council
19:27.body: ושבתך can simply mean 'your staying'. The Aramaic translation reads it as sitting down to plan, so God knows the king's plans as well as his marches.

sources.quote: וּמִיתְבָךְ בְּעֵיצָה
sources.says: The Aramaic translation renders it 'your sitting in counsel'.

sources.quote: תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: וּמִיתְבָךְ בְּעֵצָה
sources.says: Rashi quotes that translation.

sources.quote: שבתך בארצך וצאתך מארצך ובואך
sources.says: Radak gives the plain reading: your staying in your own land.

19:28.headline: Your roar, or your smugness?
19:28.body: ושאננך looks like שאנן, 'at ease'. Rashi reads it as שאון, 'roar'. Radak allows both: the king raged because he felt so secure.

sources.quote: וְשַׁאֲנַנְךָ. כְּמוֹ וּשְׁאוֹנְךָ
sources.says: Rashi says it means 'your roar'.

sources.quote: ויש לפרשו כמשמעו בעבור כי התרגזו היה בעבור שהיה שלו שקט ושאנן
sources.says: Radak says it can also keep its plain sense, 'your complacency', since his rage came from feeling safe.

19:28.headline: A ring for an unruly animal, or a hook for a fish?
19:28.body: God says He will put His חח in the king's nose. Rashi sees a ring used to lead a bad-tempered beast. Radak sees a bent iron hook that pulls a fish from the water.

sources.quote: כְּמִין שִׁיר הוּא, שֶׁמּוֹשְׁכִין בּוֹ בְּהֵמָה שֶׁעֲסָקֶיהָ רָעִים
sources.says: Rashi says it is a ring used to pull an animal that behaves badly.

sources.quote: הוא הברזל כמין מחט וראשו כפוף נוקב אף הדג ולחיו ומעלין אותו מן המים
sources.says: Radak says it is an iron like a needle with a bent tip that pierces a fish's nose and jaw to lift it from the water.

19:29.headline: A one-time word for what grows back on its own
19:29.body: סחיש has no close match elsewhere. It is read as the second wild growth from fallen seed, or new shoots from cut-down trees.

sources.quote: סחיש. ענינו ספיחי ספיחים, או ספיחי האילנות, ואין לו דומה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means growth from earlier wild growth, or the regrowth of trees, and that the word has no parallel.

sources.quote: סָחִישׁ. גְּדוּעֵי אִילָנוֹת שֶׁיִּצְמְחוּ
sources.says: Rashi says it is cut-down trees that sprout again.

19:31.headline: 'Of hosts' is read aloud but not written here
19:31.body: The written text says only 'the zeal of the LORD'. Tradition adds צבאות, 'of hosts', when reading it aloud.

sources.quote: קנאת ה' צבאות. קרי ולא כתיב
sources.says: Radak notes that the word צבאות is read but not written.

19:35.headline: Why 'dead corpses'? A living body can also be a פגר
19:35.body: The verse says the soldiers were פגרים מתים, 'dead bodies'. Ralbag explains the extra word: פגר can also mean a living body.

sources.quote: והנה פגרים מתים הם גופי' מתים כי הגוף החי יקרא גם כן פגר
sources.says: Ralbag says the phrase means dead bodies, since a living body is also called פגר.

19:37.headline: The god Nisroch is read as a plank from Noah's ark
19:37.body: נסרך sounds like נסר, a plank. Rashi says the Assyrian king worshipped a plank from Noah's ark, and was killed while bowing to it.

sources.quote: נֶסֶר מִתֵּבָתוֹ שֶׁל נֹחַ
sources.says: Rashi says Nisroch was a plank from Noah's ark.

sources.quote: נסר מתיבתו של נח היה לו לאלוה
sources.says: Metzudat David says the king treated a plank from Noah's ark as his god.

2:3.headline: Taken 'from over your head', like a crown
2:3.body: The disciples say God will take Elijah 'from over your head'. Metzudat David says Elijah was like a crown on Elisha's head. Ralbag says it means Elijah was taken away from Elisha, not that he died.

sources.quote: הנה היה לך לעטרה, ויוסר העטרה מעל ראשך
sources.says: Metzudat David says Elijah was a crown to Elisha, and the crown will be taken from his head.

sources.quote: וזה יורה שלא לקחו אלהים במוחלט אבל לקחו מעם אלישע
sources.says: Ralbag says this shows God did not take Elijah away entirely, only away from Elisha.

2:12.headline: 'My father, my father': Elisha calls his teacher 'father'
2:12.body: Elijah was not Elisha's father. The Targum and Radak read אבי as 'my master'. Ralbag says a teacher is called a father because he gives birth to the student's mind.

sources.quote: אבי אבי. כתרגומו רבי רבי וכן תלמידי הנביאים נקראו בני הנביאים
sources.says: Radak says it means 'my master, my master', as the Targum has it, just as disciples are called 'sons of the prophets'.

sources.quote: כן הרב יקרא אב כי הוא המוליד שכל התלמיד
sources.says: Ralbag says a teacher is called a father because he brings the student's mind into being.

2:12.headline: Elijah was Israel's 'chariots and horsemen'
2:12.body: Elisha calls Elijah the chariots and horsemen of Israel. The Targum, quoted by Rashi, says his prayers did more for Israel than chariots and horsemen. Ralbag says he was Israel's strength in war.

sources.quote: רַבִּי רַבִּי דְּטָב לְהוֹן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל בִּצְלוֹתֵהּ מֵרְתִיכִין וּפָרָשִׁין
sources.says: Rashi quotes the Targum: my master, whose prayer was better for Israel than chariots and horsemen.

sources.quote: כאילו יאמר שהוא התוקף והחוזק של ישראל במלחמ'
sources.says: Ralbag says it means Elijah was Israel's might and strength in battle.

2:14.headline: 'Where is the God of Elijah?': a question, or a prayer?
2:14.body: Read plainly, Elisha asks where God is, since the water did not part. The Targum turns it into a prayer: 'Accept my plea, LORD God of Elijah'.

sources.quote: תרגום יונתן כן ואמר קבל בעותי ה' אלהיה דאליהו ולפי פשוטו איה הוא שאינו מראה כח האות לי
sources.says: Radak says the Targum reads it as 'accept my prayer', while the plain sense is 'where is He', since no sign had come.

2:17.headline: They pressed him 'until shame', or 'until long delay'?
2:17.body: Rashi reads בש as shame: Elisha was embarrassed to keep refusing. Metzudat Zion reads it as delay, as in 'they waited until it was late'.

sources.quote: נִתְבַּיֵּשׁ מֵהֶם, שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמְרוּ אֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה לְהַקְבִּיל פְּנֵי רַבּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says he was ashamed before them, so they would not say he did not want his master back.

sources.quote: בוש. ענין איחור, כמו (שופטים ג כה): ויחילו עד בוש
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says בוש means delay, as in 'they waited until it was late' in Judges.

2:19.headline: If the water kills, why is the town called 'good'?
2:19.body: The people say Jericho's site is good but its water is bad. Rashi asks what was good about it. He answers with the rabbis' saying: a place has charm for those who live there.

sources.quote: אִם כֵּן מַהוּ: וּמוֹשַׁב הָעִיר טוֹב, מִכָּאן אָמְרוּ: חֵן מָקוֹם עַל יוֹשְׁבָיו
sources.says: Rashi asks why the site is called good, and answers that a place is charming to its own people.

2:21.headline: Salt spoils water, yet salt healed it
2:21.body: Elisha throws salt into the spring to make the water good. Rashi and Radak note that salt makes water worse, so this was a miracle inside a miracle.

sources.quote: וַהֲלֹא מֶלַח דָּבָר הַמְקַלְקֵל אֶת הַמַּיִם הוּא, אֶלָּא נֵס בְּתוֹךְ נֵס
sources.says: Rashi says salt ruins water, so this was a miracle within a miracle.

sources.quote: נס בתוך נס היה כי המלח עושה המים רעים
sources.says: Radak says it was a miracle within a miracle, because salt makes water bad.

2:23.headline: 'Little boys': the rabbis hear 'empty of good deeds'
2:23.body: The boys who mocked Elisha are called נערים קטנים. The rabbis read נערים as מנוערים, 'emptied' of good deeds, and קטנים as 'small in faith'.

sources.quote: ורז"ל דרשו נערים שהיו מנוערים מן המצות קטנים שהיו מקטני אמנה
sources.says: Radak cites the rabbis: נערים means emptied of commandments, and קטנים means small in faith.

sources.quote: הַמְנֹעָרִין מִן הַמִּצְוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says they were emptied of commandments.

20:1.headline: "You will die and not live": why say it twice?
20:1.body: Radak gives the plain sense: you will not recover from this illness. Rashi gives the sages' reading: you will die in this world and not live in the next, because you never married. Radak notes that Hezekiah's sons were in fact born after this illness.

sources.quote: לא תרפא מחולי זה כי מתוך זה החולי תמות
sources.says: Radak says it means you will not be healed of this illness, and you will die from it.

sources.quote: כִּי מֵת אַתָּה. בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
sources.says: Rashi says "you will die" refers to this world.

sources.quote: לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא נָסַבְתְּ אִשָּׁה
sources.says: Rashi says "you will not live" refers to the world to come, because Hezekiah had not married.

sources.quote: ואמת הוא כי בניו נולדו אחר חליו
sources.says: Radak says it is true that his sons were born after his illness.

20:2.headline: Which wall? The Targum says the Temple's wall
20:2.body: Hezekiah turns his face to the wall to pray. Radak says he did it to focus his heart. The Targum says it was the wall of the Temple.

sources.quote: אל הקיר. כדי לכוון לבו בתפלה
sources.says: Radak says he turned to the wall to focus his heart in prayer.

sources.quote: וְאַסְחַר יַת אַפּוֹהִי לְכוֹתֵל בֵּית מַקְדְשָׁא
sources.says: The Targum says he turned his face to the wall of the Temple.

20:3.headline: "I did what was good": he hid Solomon's book of cures
20:3.body: Hezekiah reminds God of the good he did. Radak cites a midrash: he hid away Solomon's book of cures, because people trusted it and stopped turning to God.

sources.quote: ובדרש והטוב בעיניך עשיתי שגנז ספר רפואו' שעשה שלמה והיו העם בוטחים בו ולא היו דורשים את ה' בלבם
sources.says: Radak cites a midrash that the good deed was hiding Solomon's book of cures, which people relied on instead of seeking God.

20:4.headline: Written "the city", read "the courtyard": God answered fast
20:4.body: The text is written העיר, "the city", and read חצר, "the courtyard". Isaiah had not yet left the palace when God's answer came. Rashi says God hurried to send the cure before word spread in the city that the king must die. Radak also cites a view that a royal court was as big as a small city.

sources.quote: העיר כתי' וחצר קרי
sources.says: Radak says it is written "the city" and read "the courtyard".

sources.quote: לְהוֹדִיעַ רְפוּאָתוֹ, בְּטֶרֶם יֵצֵא קוֹל הֲבָרָה בָּעִיר שֶׁנִּקְנְסָה עָלָיו מִיתָה
sources.says: Rashi says God hurried to announce the cure before a rumor went out in the city that death was decreed on him.

sources.quote: מכאן שהסרטיא של מלכים כעיירות בינוניות
sources.says: Radak cites the sages: from here we learn that a king's court is like a mid-sized town.

20:7.headline: A fig cake on the boil: a miracle inside a miracle
20:7.body: Rashi says fresh figs are תאנים, and pressed into a round cake they are a דבלה. He adds that fig cake makes even healthy flesh rot, so healing with it was a miracle inside a miracle. Ralbag says figs help a little with boils, since God likes to work miracles through some natural means.

sources.quote: כְּשֶׁהֵם לַחִין קְרוּיִין תְּאֵנִים, וּכְשֶׁנִּדְרָסִים בְּעִגּוּל קְרוּיִין דְּבֵלָה
sources.says: Rashi says when moist they are called figs, and when pressed into a round they are called דבלה.

sources.quote: וְנֵס בְּתוֹךְ נֵס, שֶׁהֲרֵי אַף בָּשָׂר חַי כְּשֶׁאַתָּה נוֹתֵן עָלָיו דְּבֵלָה, נִסְרָח
sources.says: Rashi says it was a miracle within a miracle, since even healthy flesh rots when fig cake is put on it.

sources.quote: הנה בו קצת מבוא ברפואת המורסות ובבשולם
sources.says: Ralbag says fig cake has some part in healing and ripening boils, though not the power to do this.

20:8.headline: "What is the sign?" or "What a sign it will be!"
20:8.body: Radak reads it as a question: Hezekiah asked for a sign, because the death sentence had been said twice. Metzudat Zion and Metzudat David read מה as wonder, as in "how majestic is Your name": how great a sign this will be.

sources.quote: מה אות. שאל אות לפי שאמר לו הגזרה כפולה
sources.says: Radak says Hezekiah asked for a sign because the decree had been said to him twice.

sources.quote: מלת ׳מה׳, יורה על גודל הדבר וחשיבותו, כמו (תהלים ח ט): מה אדיר שמך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says מה shows how great and important something is, as in Psalm 8.

sources.quote: מה מאד יחשב לאות גדול ונפלא
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means: how much this will count as a great and wondrous sign.

20:9.headline: "The shadow went": jump ahead ten steps, or stay put?
20:9.body: הלך is past tense. Radak reads it as future: shall the shadow jump forward ten steps, or go back ten? Rashi reads it differently: shall the shadow stay where it is for ten hours, or go back ten steps?

sources.quote: הלך הצל. כמו ילך שאל לו באיז' אות יבחר
sources.says: Radak says הלך means "will go": Isaiah asked which sign Hezekiah would choose.

sources.quote: חָפֵץ אַתָּה שֶׁיַּמְתִּין בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁהוּא שָׁם כְּדֵי מַהֲלַךְ עֶשֶׂר שָׁעוֹת, אוֹ יָשׁוּב לְמַעְלָה עֶשֶׂר מַעֲלוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says Isaiah asked: do you want the shadow to wait where it is for ten hours, or go back up ten steps?

20:9.headline: מעלות: the steps of a sun clock, one step per hour
20:9.body: מעלות means steps. Rashi and Metzudat David say these steps were built facing the sun to tell the time. Each hour the shadow went down one step. The Targum simply says "ten hours".

sources.quote: כְּבָר יָרַד הַצֵּל לְמַעֲלוֹת הָעֲשׂוּיוֹת לִשְׁעוֹת הַיּוֹם
sources.says: Rashi says the shadow had already gone down the steps made for telling the hours of the day.

sources.quote: מעלות היו עשויות מול החמה, לבחון בהם שעות היום, כי כל שעה ירד הצל מעלה אחת
sources.says: Metzudat David says steps were built facing the sun to tell the hours, and each hour the shadow went down one step.

sources.quote: הַיְהַךְ טוּלָא עֲסַר שָׁעִין
sources.says: The Targum renders it "shall the shadow go ten hours".

20:11.headline: Ahaz's steps: ten hours taken from him, returned to his son
20:11.body: Radak says Ahaz built these steps. Rashi gives the sages' reading: the day Ahaz died, the sun set ten hours early so the wicked king would not be mourned. Now those ten hours came back for his son Hezekiah.

sources.quote: במעלות אחז. כי הוא בנה אותם המעלות
sources.says: Radak says they are called the steps of Ahaz because he built them.

sources.quote: יוֹם שֶׁמֵּת אָחָז, נִתְקַצֵּר הַיּוֹם וּמִהֵר הַצֵּל לֵירֵד עֶשֶׂר מַעֲלוֹת, כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא נִסְפָּד, וְאוֹתָן עֶשֶׂר שָׁעוֹת חָזְרוּ עַכְשָׁיו לְחִזְקִיָּהוּ
sources.says: Rashi says that on the day Ahaz died the day was cut short by ten steps so he would not be mourned, and those ten hours now returned to Hezekiah.

20:12.headline: Why Babylon cared that Hezekiah was sick: the sun turned back
20:12.body: Rashi gives a midrash. Until then no one who fell ill had recovered. The king of Babylon woke to find morning had come back, and was told that Hezekiah's God had turned the sun. Radak says the envoys came mainly to ask about that sign.

sources.quote: וְעַד אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם לֹא הָיָה אָדָם חוֹלֶה וְחָיָה
sources.says: Rashi says that until that day no one fell sick and lived.

sources.quote: אָמַר לָהֶם: מִי הֶחֱזִירוֹ, אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֱלֹהָיו שֶל חִזְקִיָּהוּ
sources.says: Rashi says the Babylonian king asked who turned the sun back, and was told: Hezekiah's God.

sources.quote: לא היה עיקר שליחותי על חליו אלא על המופת שנעשה לו על חליו
sources.says: Radak says the main purpose of the mission was not the illness but the sign done for him in it.

20:13.headline: Hezekiah "listened to them", or in Isaiah, "was glad of them"
20:13.body: Radak says עליהם here means "to them": the envoys asked to see his treasures and he agreed. He notes that Isaiah 39 has וישמח, "he was glad", instead of וישמע.

sources.quote: וישמע עליהם. כמו אליהם ועל כמו אל
sources.says: Radak says עליהם means "to them", with על in place of אל.

sources.quote: ובישעיה וישמח עליהם
sources.says: Radak notes that Isaiah has "he was glad over them".

20:13.headline: בית נכתה: his spice store, his armory, or his queen?
20:13.body: נכתה is a rare word. Rashi says it is his store of spices, like נכאת in the Joseph story. Radak gives the sages' three views: his wife served them drinks, he showed them his weapons, or he showed them his treasury.

sources.quote: בֵּית גִּנְזֵי בְּשָׂמָיו, כְּמוֹ: נְכֹאת וּצְרִי וָלֹט
sources.says: Rashi says it is the house where his spices were stored, like "gum, balm and myrrh".

sources.quote: נכתה. ענין אוצר נחמד
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means a treasure of precious things.

sources.quote: מהם אמרו אשתו היתה משקה להם ומהם אמרו זין אוכל זין הראה להם ומהם אמרו בית גנזיו הראה להם
sources.says: Radak says the sages differ: some say his wife served them drink, some say he showed them his weapons, some say his treasure house.

20:14.headline: "From a far land": Hezekiah answers the prophet with pride
20:14.body: Rashi says Hezekiah should have told Isaiah, "You are God's prophet, why ask me?" Instead he boasted that they came from far away. Rashi lists him with Cain and Balaam, three whom God tested and found wanting.

sources.quote: וּמְצָאָן עָבִיט שֶל מַיִם עֲכוּרִים, קַיִן, יְחִזְקִיָּהוּ, וּבִלְעָם
sources.says: Rashi says God tested three and found them a vessel of muddy water: Cain, Hezekiah and Balaam.

sources.quote: הִתְחִיל חִזְקִיָּה מִתְגָּאֶה וְאָמַר: מֵאֶרֶץ רְחוֹקָה בָּאוּ אֵלַי
sources.says: Rashi says Hezekiah began to boast, saying they came to him from a far land.

20:17.headline: "Nothing will be left" answers "nothing he did not show"
20:17.body: Hezekiah boasted that there was nothing, לא היה דבר, he did not show the envoys. Rashi says the punishment is measure for measure: לא יותר דבר, nothing will be left.

sources.quote: לֹא יִוָּתֵר דָּבָר. מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה, לֹא הָיָה דָּבָר
sources.says: Rashi says "nothing will be left" is measure for measure for "there was nothing he did not show".

20:18.headline: סריסים: eunuchs, or palace officials?
20:18.body: סריס can mean a eunuch or a court officer. The Targum and Metzudat Zion say officers. Radak gives a dispute of the sages: real eunuchs, or that idolatry was made barren in their days, when all saw it had no power.

sources.quote: סריסים. שרים וממונים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says סריסים means officers and officials.

sources.quote: מהם אמרו סריסים ממש ומה' אמרו שנסתרס' ע"ג בימיהם כלומר שהכירו הכל שאין בה ממש
sources.says: Radak says some sages said real eunuchs, and some said idolatry was made barren in their days, as all saw it had no substance.

sources.quote: וי"ת רברבין כמו שרים
sources.says: Radak says the Targum renders it "great ones", meaning officers.

23:2.headline: Prophets at Josiah's reading, or scribes? The Targum says scribes
23:2.body: Targum Jonathan turns "the prophets" into "the scribes", meaning students. Radak explains why: the king had just sent to Huldah, which suggests no other prophets were at hand. Radak also allows the plain sense, since Jeremiah and Zephaniah were prophets then.

sources.quote: ת"י וכהניא וספריא תרגם הנביאים סופרים כלומר תלמידים לפי שלא היו שם נביאים אחרים שהרי המלך שלח אל חולדה
sources.says: Radak says the Targum renders "prophets" as scribes, meaning students, since no other prophets were there: the king had sent to Huldah.

sources.quote: ונוכל לפרש נביאים כמשמעו כי ירמיה וצפניה בן כושי היו נביאים בזמן ההוא
sources.says: Radak says "prophets" can also be read plainly, since Jeremiah and Zephaniah son of Cushi were prophets at that time.

sources.quote: וְכַהֲנַיָא וְסַפְרַיָא
sources.says: Targum Jonathan renders it "and the priests and the scribes".

23:3.headline: The king stood "on the pillar": his set place in the Temple
23:3.body: עמוד usually means a pillar. Rashi, Metzudat David and Radak say here it is the place set aside for the king to stand in the Temple. Ralbag thinks a stand was built for him, as at the gathering where the king reads the Torah to the people.

sources.quote: מְקוֹם מַעֲמַד הַמֶּלֶךְ בְּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says it is the king's standing place in the Temple.

sources.quote: על המקום המיוחד למלך לעמוד בה
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is the place set aside for the king to stand.

sources.quote: ידמה שבנו שם עמוד והיה בו המלך בעת קראו את התורה כמו שנזכר בפרשת הקהל
sources.says: Ralbag says it seems they built a stand there for the king while he read the Torah, as in the Torah's passage on the national gathering.

sources.quote: ובדברי הימים ויעמוד המלך על עמדו כלומר במקום שהיה רגיל לעמוד שם
sources.says: Radak notes that Chronicles says "on his stand", the place where he usually stood.

23:5.headline: Kemarim: idol priests named for their black robes
23:5.body: The verse uses כמרים, not the usual word for priests. Metzudat Zion and Radak say these were idol priests who dressed in black. Radak links the name to נכמרו, "blackened", in "our skin is blackened like an oven".

sources.quote: הכמרים. הם כהני עבודה זרה הלובשים שחורים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says they are idol priests who wear black.

sources.quote: כי הכמרים הם לובשים שחורים לפיכך נקראו כמרים מענין עורנו כתנור נכמרו
sources.says: Radak says the kemarim wear black, so their name comes from "our skin is blackened like an oven".

23:7.headline: "Houses of the qedeshim": brothels, or weaving rooms for Asherah?
23:7.body: קדשים comes from the root for "holy". Metzudat Zion says the Bible uses it for anything set apart, even something forbidden. Rashi reads these as houses of lewdness. Radak objects that such houses would not stand in God's Temple: they were rooms where women wove hangings for the Asherah.

sources.quote: הקדשים. דבר המובדל מן האדם, ואף בעבור הטומאה והאיסור, נקרא בלשון קודש
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says something set apart from people is called by the word "holy", even when it is set apart for being impure or forbidden.

sources.quote: אֶת בָּתֵּי הַקְּדֵשִׁים. בָּתֵּי הַזִּמָּה
sources.says: Rashi says they were houses of lewdness.

sources.quote: כי אם היה הקדשים זה ענין זמה מה ענין בבית ה' אבל האשרה שעשה מנשה בבית ה' עשה שם בתים לנשים שיארגו יריעות לכבוד האשרה
sources.says: Radak asks what lewdness would be doing in God's house, and says Manasseh made rooms there for women to weave hangings in honor of the Asherah.

23:7.headline: The women wove "houses" for Asherah: hangings, not buildings
23:7.body: No one weaves a house. Rashi, Metzudat David and Radak say these בתים were woven hangings. Metzudat David and Radak compare the "houses" that held the poles of the Tabernacle: the hangings around the Asherah made a house for it.

sources.quote: אֹרְגוֹת שָׁם בָּתִּים. יְרִיעוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says the "houses" were curtains.

sources.quote: רצה לומר: יריעות לתלות סביבה, ודוגמתו (שמות לז יד): בתים לבדים
sources.says: Metzudat David says they were curtains to hang around it, like the "houses for the poles" in Exodus.

sources.quote: יריעות היו אורגות שם והיריעות היו בתים לאשרה כמו בתים לבדים
sources.says: Radak says they wove curtains there, and the curtains were "houses" for the Asherah, like the "houses for the poles".

23:10.headline: Topheth was named for drums that drowned out the children's cries
23:10.body: Topheth was where children were passed through fire to Molech. Rashi, Metzudat David and Radak say it took its name from תפים, drums. The priests beat drums so the father would not hear his son's cries and take pity.

sources.quote: וְעַל שֵׁם שֶׁהָיוּ הַכֹּהֲנִים מַקִּישִׁים בְּתֻפִּים, שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁמַע הָאָב אֶת נַהֲמַת הַבֵּן
sources.says: Rashi says it was named because the priests beat drums so the father would not hear his son groan.

sources.quote: ונקראה כן על שם שהיו מכים בתופים, לבל ישמע האב נהמת הבן כשהוא נשרף בין המדורות, ולבל יכמרו רחמיו
sources.says: Metzudat David says it was so called because they beat drums, so the father would not hear his son's groans as he burned and be moved to pity.

sources.quote: ואמרו כי נקרא כן כי היו מרקדים ומכים בתופים בשעת העבודה
sources.says: Radak says it was so called because they danced and beat drums during the rite.

23:11.headline: Parvarim: Rashi says plainly that he does not know
23:11.body: Rashi admits it: "I do not know what they are." Metzudat Zion and Radak say פרורים are the open lands around a city. They draw on the Aramaic of Ezekiel and on a saying of the sages, "Babylon and all its outskirts".

sources.quote: אֲשֶׁר בַּפַּרְוָרִים. לֹא יָדַעְתִּי מָה הֵם
sources.says: Rashi says: I do not know what they are.

sources.quote: אשר בפרורים. פירוש מגרשי הערים ותרגום ירעשו מגרשות יזועון פרורים ובדברי רז"ל בבל וכל פרורהא
sources.says: Radak says it means the open lands around cities: the Aramaic of "the open lands will shake" uses this word, and the sages speak of "Babylon and all its outskirts".

sources.quote: בפרורים. ירעשו מגרשות (יחזקאל כז כח) תרגום ירושלמי: פרוריא
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the Aramaic translation of Ezekiel's "open lands" is פרוריא.

23:13.headline: Mount of Anointing renamed Mount of the Destroyer, for shame
23:13.body: The Mount of Olives was also called הר המשחה, the Mount of Anointing. Because idol shrines were built there, the verse twists the name into הר המשחית, the Mount of the Destroyer. Rashi, Metzudat David and Radak all say so.

sources.quote: הַר הַזֵּיתִים, הוּא הַר הַמִּשְׁחָה, וְכֵיוָן שֶׁהִזְכִּיר אֶת שְׁמוֹ עַל יְדֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, שִׁנָּה שְׁמוֹ לִגְנַאי
sources.says: Rashi says it is the Mount of Olives, the Mount of Anointing; since it is named here in connection with idolatry, the verse changed its name to one of shame.

sources.quote: הוא הר המשחה, ובעבור העבודת כוכבים ומזלות כנהו לגנאי
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is the Mount of Anointing, given a shameful name because of the idolatry.

sources.quote: הר הזיתים ונקרא הר המשחה ולגנאי מפני הע"ג שהיה שם קראו הר המשחית
sources.says: Radak says the Mount of Olives was called the Mount of Anointing, and because of the idolatry there it was called, for shame, the Mount of the Destroyer.

23:25.headline: "With all his might" means with all his money
23:25.body: Metzudat Zion says מאד here means wealth, as in "love God with all your might" in Deuteronomy. Metzudat David and Radak cite the sages: Josiah paid back from his own pocket every case he had judged between the ages of eight and eighteen.

sources.quote: מאודו. עשרו, כמו (דברים ו ה): ובכל מאדך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says מאדו means his wealth, as in "with all your might" in Deuteronomy.

sources.quote: ותשובתו היתה להחזיר משלו כל דין שדן מבן שמונה עד שמונה עשרה, וזה שנאמר: ובכל מאודו
sources.says: Metzudat David says his repentance was to repay from his own money every judgment he gave from age eight to eighteen, and that is "with all his might".

sources.quote: תלמוד לומר ובכל מאודו שהחזיר להם משלו
sources.says: Radak says that is why it says "with all his might": he repaid them from his own money.

23:29.headline: Pharaoh Necho: the Targum calls him "the lame"
23:29.body: Targum Jonathan translates the name נכה as "the lame one". Metzudat Zion and Radak explain: נכה means broken or crippled, as in "a son lame in his feet" in Samuel.

sources.quote: נכה. תרגם יונתן: חגירא, והוא מענין שבירה, וכן (שמואל ב ד ד): בן נכה רגלים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says Jonathan translates it "the lame", from the sense of breaking, as in "lame in his feet" in Samuel.

sources.quote: פרעה נכה. כתרגומו פרעה חגירא שהיה נכה רגלים
sources.says: Radak says, as the Targum has it, it means Pharaoh the lame, for he was lame in his feet.

sources.quote: פַּרְעֹה חֲגִירָא מַלְכָּא דְמִצְרַיִם
sources.says: Targum Jonathan renders it "Pharaoh the lame, king of Egypt".

23:29.headline: Killed "when he saw him": when the two met in battle
23:29.body: Josiah was not killed at a glance. Metzudat David says "seeing" here means facing each other in battle, as in "they looked one another in the face" earlier in Kings. Radak says Pharaoh killed him when he saw Josiah meant to fight, dressed for war.

sources.quote: רצה לומר: בהלחמו עמו, וכמו (לעיל יד יא): ויתראו פנים, שרצה לומר: נלחמו פנים בפנים
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means when he fought him, as in "they looked each other in the face", which means they fought face to face.

sources.quote: ופי' כראותו אותו כשראה אותו שדעתו להלחם עמו שהתרה בו וראה אותו לבוש כלי מלחמה
sources.says: Radak says it means when Pharaoh saw that Josiah meant to fight him, after he had warned him, and saw him dressed in armor.

23:30.headline: Why anoint a king's son? His older brother was passed over
23:30.body: A king's son who follows his father is not anointed. Rashi and Radak say Jehoahaz was anointed because his brother Jehoiakim was two years older. When the throne is in dispute, anointing settles it, as with Solomon and with Joash.

sources.quote: לֹא הָיָה צָרִיךְ מְשִׁיחָה, אֶלָּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָיָה יְהוֹיָקִים אָחִיו גָּדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים
sources.says: Rashi says he did not need anointing, except that his brother Jehoiakim was two years older.

sources.quote: והלא אין מושחין מלך בן מלך ולא משחו שלמה אלא מפני מחלוקתו של אדוניהו ואת יהואש מפני מחלוקתו של עתליה
sources.says: Radak says a king's son is not anointed; Solomon was anointed only because of Adonijah's challenge, and Joash because of Athaliah's.

sources.quote: ידמה שמשחו אותו מפני המחלק' שהיתה בין האחים
sources.says: Ralbag says it seems they anointed him because of the dispute between the brothers.

23:33.headline: Written "while he reigned", read "from reigning": two readings
23:33.body: The text is written במלך, "while he was king", but read ממלך, "from being king". Radak explains both: Pharaoh seized him during his short reign in Jerusalem, and removed him from the throne. Metzudat David follows the reading: to remove him from reigning in Jerusalem.

sources.quote: במלך בירושלם. כן כתיב רוצה לומר בעוד מלכו בירושלם מעט הזמן הזה לקחו וקרי ממלוך שהסירו מהמלוכה
sources.says: Radak says it is written במלך, meaning Pharaoh took him while he still reigned in Jerusalem for that short time, and read ממלוך, meaning he removed him from the kingship.

sources.quote: ממלוך. להסירו ממלוך בירושלים
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means to remove him from reigning in Jerusalem.

25:4.headline: "The city was breached" almost by itself, because of hunger
25:4.body: The verb is passive, so the verse does not say who did it. Radak and Ralbag say the Chaldean army broke through. Metzudat David adds that it was as if the wall broke by itself, since Jerusalem's men were too weak from hunger to resist.

sources.quote: חיל נבוכדנצאר בקעו חומתה, וכאלו נעשית מעצמה, כי אנשי ירושלים היו חלושים ברעב, ולא עמדו למולם לעכב על ידם
sources.says: Metzudat David says Nebuchadnezzar's army broke through its wall, as if it happened by itself, since Jerusalem's men were weak from hunger and did not stand against them to stop them.

sources.quote: בקעו הכשדים חומת העיר וכיון שראו אנשי המלחמה אשר בעיר כי בקעו העיר ברחו בלילה ההוא
sources.says: Radak says the Chaldeans broke the city wall, and when the soldiers in the city saw it breached they fled that night.

sources.quote: ותבקע העיר. ר"ל על ידי חיל כשדים
sources.says: Ralbag says the city was breached by the Chaldean army.

25:4.headline: "Between the two walls": a gate, or a tunnel and a deer?
25:4.body: Plainly it is a gate between two walls, by the king's garden. Rashi passes on a midrash: it was a tunnel from Zedekiah's house to the plains of Jericho, and God sent a deer over it, which led the Chaldeans to him.

sources.quote: בדרך השער העומד בין שתי החומות אשר אצל גן המלך
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is the way of the gate standing between the two walls beside the king's garden.

sources.quote: ר"ל שיצאו דרך שהיה בין שתי חומות כדי שלא יראום כשדים ולא ירגישו בהם
sources.says: Ralbag says they left by a road between two walls so the Chaldeans would not see or notice them.

sources.quote: מְעָרָה הוֹלֶכֶת מִבֵּיתוֹ עַד עַרְבוֹת יְרִיחוֹ, וּבָרַח לוֹ דֶּרֶךְ הַמְּעָרָה, וְהַקָּבָּ"ה זִמֵּן צְבִי הוֹלֵךְ עַל גַּג הַמְּעָרָה חוּץ לָעִיר
sources.says: Rashi says it was a cave running from his house to the plains of Jericho, that he fled through it, and that God arranged for a deer to walk over the cave outside the city.

25:8.headline: Seventh here, tenth in Jeremiah: how the Temple burned
25:8.body: Jeremiah says the 10th. The sages say the nations entered the Temple on the 7th, spoiled it on the 8th and 9th, set it on fire near dusk on the 9th, and it burned until the end of the 10th.

sources.quote: בשבעה בו נכנסו גוים להיכל ואכלו ושתו וקלקלו בו שמיני ותשיעי ובתשיעי סמוך לחשכה הציתו בו את האור והיה דולק והולך עד סוף עשירי
sources.says: Radak says the sages explained that on the seventh the nations entered the Temple, ate and drank and spoiled it on the eighth and ninth, and near dark on the ninth set it on fire, and it burned until the end of the tenth.

sources.quote: וידמה שהתחלת החרבן היה בשבעה לחדש כי אז נכנסו בירושלם וסוף החורבן היה בעשור לחדש כי אז נשרף בית המקדש
sources.says: Ralbag says it seems the destruction began on the seventh, when they entered Jerusalem, and ended on the tenth, when the Temple was burned.

25:9.headline: "Every great house": synagogues, or the houses of the great?
25:9.body: Rashi reads בית גדול as the synagogues, where Torah and prayer are made great, as well as the nobles' houses. Radak and the Aramaic translation read it only as the houses of great men.

sources.quote: וְאֶת כָּל בֵּית גָּדוֹל. בָּתֵּי כְּנֵסִיּוֹת שֶׁמְּגַדְּלִין בָּהֶן תּוֹרָה וּתְפִלָּה וּבָתֵּי הַשָּׂרִים
sources.says: Rashi says "every great house" means the synagogues in which they magnify Torah and prayer, and the houses of the nobles.

sources.quote: כל בית אדם גדול ר"ל בתי הגדולים וכן ת"י בתי רברביא
sources.says: Radak says it means every house of a great man, the houses of the great, and so Targum Jonathan says "houses of the nobles".

sources.quote: וְיַת כָּל בָּתֵּי רַבְרְבַיָא
sources.says: Targum Jonathan renders it "and all the houses of the nobles".

25:11.headline: "The fallen" are those who went over to the enemy
25:11.body: In this verse הנפלים does not mean people killed in battle. Rashi, Metzudat Zion and Radak say these were people who left the city and gave themselves up to Babylon. The Aramaic translation calls them "those who obeyed".

sources.quote: שֶׁשָּׁמְעוּ לְקוֹל נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר וְיָצְאוּ אֵלָיו מִן הָעִיר
sources.says: Rashi says they are those who listened to Nebuchadnezzar's voice and went out to him from the city.

sources.quote: הם היוצאים מעצמן, למסור עצמן ולשכון בינותם, וכן (ירמיהו לז יג): אל הכשדים אתה נופל
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says they are those who went out on their own to hand themselves over and live among them, like "you are falling away to the Chaldeans" in Jeremiah.

sources.quote: שיצאו אליו קודם כבוש העיר ומסרו עצמם אליו
sources.says: Radak says they went out to him before the city was taken and handed themselves over to him.

sources.quote: וְיַת שְׁמִיעַיָא דְאִשְׁתַּמָעוּ עַל מַלְכָּא דְבָבֶל
sources.says: Targum Jonathan renders it "and those who obeyed, who obeyed the king of Babylon".

25:12.headline: "Diggers" in the plain sense; to the sages, hunters of the chilazon
25:12.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion read it as diggers, tied to pits and wine vats. Radak passes on the sages: the "vinedressers" were balsam gatherers from Ein Gedi to Ramah, and the "diggers" were hunters of the chilazon from the Ladder of Tyre to Haifa.

sources.quote: חוֹפְרֵי הָאָרֶץ, לְשׁוֹן יְקָבִים, שֶׁהֵם חֲפִירוֹת בַּקַּרְקַע
sources.says: Rashi says they are diggers of the ground, from the word for wine vats, which are dug in the ground.

sources.quote: ענין בורות, כמו (לעיל ג טז): עשה הנחל הזה גבים גבים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means pits, like "make this wadi full of ditches" earlier in Kings.

sources.quote: ובדברי רבותינו ז"ל תני רב יוסף לכורמים אלו מלקטי אפרסמון מעין גדי עד רמתא וליוגבים אלו צדי חלזון מסולמא דצור עד חיפא
sources.says: Radak says that in the sages' words Rav Yosef taught that the vinedressers are balsam gatherers from Ein Gedi to Ramah, and the diggers are hunters of the chilazon from the Ladder of Tyre to Haifa.

25:18.headline: "Keepers of the saf": doorkeepers, or keepers of the vessels?
25:18.body: Metzudat Zion says סף is a doorpost, so these are the gatekeepers. Radak says they kept the Temple's vessels.

sources.quote: שומרי הסף. הם השוערים, כי מזוזת השער יקרא סף, כמו (יחזקאל מ ז): וסף השער
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the keepers of the saf are the gatekeepers, since a gatepost is called a saf, as in "and the threshold of the gate" in Ezekiel.

sources.quote: שומרי הסף. שומרי כלי בית המקדש
