sources.says: Radak says the keepers of the saf are the keepers of the Temple's vessels.

25:19.headline: Five men here, seven in Jeremiah: three explanations
25:19.body: Radak says two of the seven were less important, so they are left out here. Malbim says five were found first and two more later. Radak also reports a saying of the sages that the two extra were scribes of the judges.

sources.quote: ובירמיהו אומר שבעה אנשים מראי פני המלך השנים לא היו גדולים כמו החמשה לפיכך לא מנאן כאן
sources.says: Radak says Jeremiah says seven men who saw the king's face, and the two were not as great as the five, so they are not counted here.

sources.quote: וחמשה אנשים ובירמיה ושבעה אנשים, י"ל שתחלה מצא חמשה ואחר כך מצא עוד שנים עד שהיו שבעה
sources.says: Malbim says "five men" here and "seven men" in Jeremiah can be explained by saying he first found five and then found two more, making seven.

sources.quote: כתוב אחד אומר חמשה וכתוב אחד אומר שבעה להביא שני סופרי הדיינין
sources.says: Radak says in the sages' words one verse says five and one says seven, to include the two scribes of the judges.

25:27.headline: 27th here, 25th in Jeremiah: when Nebuchadnezzar died
25:27.body: The sages say Nebuchadnezzar died on the 25th and was buried on the 26th. On the 27th Evil-Merodach dug him up, to cancel his decrees according to Rashi, or from fear that he might return according to Radak.

sources.quote: אֶלָּא בְּעֶשְׂרִים וַחֲמִשָּׁה מֵת נְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּר, וְנִקְבַּר בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְשִׁשָּׁה, בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְשִׁבְעָה הוֹצִיאוֹ אֱוִיל מְרוֹדַךְ מִקִּבְרוֹ וּגְרָרוּהוּ, בִּשְׁבִיל לְבַטֵּל גְּזֵרוֹתָיו
sources.says: Rashi says Nebuchadnezzar died on the 25th, was buried on the 26th, and on the 27th Evil-Merodach took him out of his grave and dragged him, to cancel his decrees.

sources.quote: בכ"ה מת נבוכדנצר בכ"ו נקבר בכ"ז הוציאו אויל מרודך בנו מקברו כי פחד שמא ישוב עדיין
sources.says: Radak says the sages explained that Nebuchadnezzar died on the 25th, was buried on the 26th, and on the 27th his son Evil-Merodach took him out of his grave, because he feared he might still return.

25:29.headline: "Bread before him": did Jehoiachin eat at the king's table?
25:29.body: Metzudat David says "before him" means together with him. Radak says it cannot mean at his table, since the next verse says he was given a daily allowance. Ralbag leaves both open.

sources.quote: לפניו. רצה לומר: עמו יחד
sources.says: Metzudat David says "before him" means with him together.

sources.quote: לפניו. לא לפניו ועל שולחנו שהרי אומר ארוחת תמיד נתנה לו מאת המלך דבר יום ביומו
sources.says: Radak says it does not mean before him and at his table, for it says a regular allowance was given to him from the king, each day's portion on its day.

sources.quote: אחשוב כי הוא היה מאוכלי שולחנו ועכ"ז היה שולח לו ארוחה ומשאת לפרנס ב"ב ואפשר שהוא לא היה מאוכלי שולחנו
sources.says: Ralbag says he thinks Jehoiachin was one of those who ate at the king's table and was also sent an allowance to support his household, but that possibly he was not one of those who ate at his table.

25:30.headline: ארחה means a fixed allowance of food, which fed his household
25:30.body: Metzudat Zion says the word means a fixed portion, like "an allowance and a gift" in Jeremiah. Metzudat David says it never stopped, and fed Jehoiachin's household, since he himself ate at the king's table.

sources.quote: וארחתו. הוא ענין פרס קבוע, וכן (ירמיהו מ ה): ארחה ומשאת
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says ארחתו is a fixed portion, as in "an allowance and a gift" in Jeremiah 40.

sources.quote: פרס הנתונה לו, היתה פרס הנתונה תמיד מבלי הפסק, והיה למאכל לאנשי ביתו, כי הוא בעצמו אכל לחם לפני המלך תמיד
sources.says: Metzudat David says the portion given to him was given always without stopping, and it was food for his household, since he himself ate bread before the king always.

25:30.headline: "All the days of his life": whose life?
25:30.body: Radak says Rav and Levi disagreed: one said the days of Evil-Merodach's life, the other the days of Jehoiachin's life. Ralbag says we cannot decide.

sources.quote: ובדברי רז"ל רב ולוי חד אמר ימי חיו של אויל מרודך וחד אמר ימי חייו של יהויכין
sources.says: Radak says in the sages' words Rav and Levi disagree, one saying the days of Evil-Merodach's life and one the days of Jehoiachin's life.

sources.quote: אפשר ששב אל יהויכין ואפשר ששב אל אויל מרודך ואין לנו הכרע בזה
sources.says: Ralbag says it may refer to Jehoiachin and it may refer to Evil-Merodach, and we have no way to decide.

3:4.headline: Mesha was a 'speckler': a sheep master named for spotted flocks
3:4.body: נקד is a rare word for a flock owner. Metzudat David and Radak say it comes from נקודים, speckled, because most sheep are spotted. Amos was called the same thing.

sources.quote: בעל צאן הרבה, ועל שרובם נקודים, יקרא המתעסק בהם בשם נוקד
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means an owner of many sheep, named נוקד because most of them are speckled.

sources.quote: ונקרא בעל המקנה נוקד שהצאן נקודים ברוב
sources.says: Radak says the flock owner is called נוקד because sheep are mostly speckled.

3:4.headline: He 'returned' tribute: he paid it again and again
3:4.body: The verse says Mesha 'returned' sheep to Israel's king, not that he gave them. Metzudat David and Malbim say the word shows it was paid over and over, every year.

sources.quote: לפי שבכל שנה העלה לו המס הזה, לכן אמר והשיב, רצה לומר: נתן וחזר ונתן
sources.says: Metzudat David says he paid this tax every year, so the verse says 'returned': he gave and gave again.

sources.quote: כי השיב שכל שנה ושנה היה נותן מס הזה ולכן אמר לשון השבה
sources.says: Malbim says he paid this tax each year, which is why the word for returning is used.

3:11.headline: Elisha 'poured water on Elijah's hands': he served him
3:11.body: Pouring water on a master's hands means serving him. Radak cites the rabbis: the verse says 'poured', not 'learned', because serving a teacher is greater than learning from him. A midrash says water poured from Elisha's fingers on Mount Carmel.

sources.quote: ובדברי רז"ל למד לא נאמר אלא יצק מלמד ששמושה גדול מלמודה
sources.says: Radak cites the rabbis: it says 'poured' and not 'learned', teaching that serving is greater than studying.

sources.quote: וּבִיצִיקָתוֹ נַעֲשׂוּ אֶצְבְּעוֹתָיו כְּמַעְיְנוֹת מַיִם
sources.says: Rashi says that on Mount Carmel, as he poured, his fingers became springs of water.

3:12.headline: Why is Jehoshaphat not called 'king' here?
3:12.body: The verse names the king of Israel and the king of Edom by title, but Jehoshaphat only by name. Radak cites a midrash: out of humility he came down to the prophet in plain clothes, not royal robes.

sources.quote: למה לא נאמר ביהושפט מלך להודיע ענוותנותו של אותו צדיק שלא רצה לירד לפני הנביא בבגדי מלכות
sources.says: Radak says Jehoshaphat is not called king to show his humility: he would not come before the prophet in royal clothes.

sources.quote: ויהושפט פי' שלבש בגדי הדיוט בל יתהדר לפני הנביא
sources.says: Malbim says Jehoshaphat dressed as a commoner so as not to show off before the prophet.

3:13.headline: 'No!' or 'Please'? The king's reply to Elisha
3:13.body: Elisha tells the king to go to his parents' prophets. The king answers אל. Radak reads it as 'do not say that now'. The Targum reads it as a plea: please, do not recall our sins.

sources.quote: אל תאמר עתה לנו דברים אלו
sources.says: Radak says it means 'do not say these things to us now'.

sources.quote: בְּבָעוּ לָא תִּדְכַּר חוֹבִין רִשְׁעָתָא הַהִיא
sources.says: Rashi quotes the Targum: please, do not recall the sins of that wickedness.

3:15.headline: Why Elisha called for a musician before he could prophesy
3:15.body: Elisha asks for a musician, and only then does God's hand come on him. Rashi says his anger at the king had driven prophecy away. Radak adds that prophecy comes only with joy.

sources.quote: מִפְּנֵי הַכַּעַס נִסְתַּלְּקָה שְׁכִינָה מִמֶּנּוּ
sources.says: Rashi says because of his anger the divine presence left him.

sources.quote: ורוח הקדש אינה שורה אלא מתוך שמחה
sources.says: Radak says the holy spirit rests on a person only through joy.

3:15.headline: 'The hand of the LORD' means a prophetic vision
3:15.body: God has no hand. Maimonides says 'the hand of the LORD' is one name for the waking vision of prophecy, and cites this verse.

sources.quote: והיא הנקראת "מראה הנבואה", ונקראת גם "יד ה'"
sources.says: Maimonides says the prophetic vision is also called 'the hand of the LORD', citing this verse.

3:19.headline: 'Make the fields hurt' with stones
3:19.body: תכאבו means to cause pain. Here it is said of fields ruined with stones. Metzudat David and Radak say the word is borrowed from living things that feel pain.

sources.quote: והוא לשון מושאל מן בעלי חיים, הנכאבים בהשחתה
sources.says: Metzudat David says the word is borrowed from living creatures, which feel pain when harmed.

sources.quote: תכאיבו באבנים. על דרך השאלה
sources.says: Radak says it is used as a figure of speech.

3:20.headline: 'In the morning, as the offering went up': which offering?
3:20.body: Radak reads it as the morning offering. Rashi and a midrash read it as two times: rain fell in Edom in the morning and reached the camp at the afternoon offering.

sources.quote: ופירוש בבקר בעת עלות מנחת הבקר
sources.says: Radak says 'in the morning' means at the time of the morning offering.

sources.quote: הַמַּיִם הִתְחִילוּ לֵירֵד מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם בַּבֹּקֶר בְּאֶרֶץ אֱדוֹם
sources.says: Rashi says the rain began in the land of Edom in the morning and reached the valley at the afternoon offering.

3:25.headline: The 'slingers' here worked siege engines, not hand slings
3:25.body: הקלעים appears only here. Radak says these were not slings held in the hand but machines that threw heavy stones to break the wall.

sources.quote: והקלעים האלה לא היו קלעים ביד אלא קלעים שמשליכים אבנים גדולות
sources.says: Radak says these were not hand slings but devices that hurled large stones.

3:27.headline: Whose firstborn son did the king of Moab burn?
3:27.body: The verse says 'his firstborn son'. A midrash in Rashi says Mesha sacrificed his own son, copying Abraham. Radak's father says it was the son of the king of Edom, held by Moab.

sources.quote: אָמַר לָהֶם: אַף אֲנִי בֵּן בְּכוֹר יֵשׁ לִי, אֵלֵךְ וְאַקְרִיבֶנּוּ
sources.says: Rashi quotes a midrash: Mesha said he too had a firstborn son and would offer him up.

sources.quote: פי' אדוני אבי ז"ל כי בן מלך אדום הראוי למלוך תחתיו היה ברשות מלך מואב
sources.says: Radak cites his father: the heir of the king of Edom was in the king of Moab's hands.

3:27.headline: 'On the wall' is spelled like 'to the sun'
3:27.body: החמה here means the wall, but it is written without the letter vav, so it looks like חמה, the sun. Rashi and Radak say this hints that the king of Moab worshipped the sun.

sources.quote: עַל הַחֹמָה. חָסֵר וָא"ו, שֶׁהָיָה עוֹבֵד לַחַמָּה
sources.says: Rashi says it is missing a vav because he worshipped the sun.

sources.quote: ומפני זה חסר וי"ו החמה כי היה עובד לחמה
sources.says: Radak says the vav is missing from החמה because he worshipped the sun.

3:27.headline: 'Great anger against Israel': whose anger?
3:27.body: The verse does not say who was angry. Metzudat David and Radak say the king of Edom was angry at Israel. Rashi says Israel's own sins were remembered against them.

sources.quote: מלך אדום קצף על ישראל, כי בעבורה באה לו הרעה ההיא
sources.says: Metzudat David says the king of Edom was angry at Israel, since the harm came to him through them.

sources.quote: שֶׁנִּזְכְּרוּ עֲוֹנוֹתֵיהֶם, שֶׁאַף הֵם עוֹבְדִין לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
sources.says: Rashi says their sins were remembered, since they too served idols.

4:1.headline: The creditor was the king, charging interest
4:1.body: The sages say this widow's husband was Obadiah, who fed the hidden prophets with borrowed money. The lender was King Yehoram, who charged him interest. Radak adds that Yehoram was later shot 'between his arms' for stretching them out to take it.

sources.quote: הוּא יְהוֹרָם בֶּן אַחְאָב, שֶׁהָיָה מַלְוֵהוּ בְּרִבִּית
sources.says: Rashi brings the midrash that the creditor was Yehoram son of Ahab, who lent her husband money at interest to feed the prophets.

sources.quote: עַבְדָךְ עוֹבַדְיָה בַעֲלִי מִית
sources.says: The Targum names her dead husband as Obadiah.

sources.quote: ופשט זרועותיו ליטול רבית
sources.says: Radak brings the midrash that Yehoram was struck between his arms because he stretched them out to take interest.

4:2.headline: A jug named for anointing
4:2.body: אסוך appears only here. Rashi says it is just enough oil to anoint with, from סוך, to anoint. Rashi thinks the alef belongs to the root, and Radak thinks it was added.

sources.quote: כְּדֵי סִיכַת שֶׁמֶן
sources.says: Rashi says it means enough oil for anointing, and the alef is part of the root.

sources.quote: והאל"ף נוספת והוא מן סוך
sources.says: Radak says it is a jug of oil, the alef is added, and the word comes from 'anoint', because people anoint from it.

sources.quote: ויקרא כן על שם שסכין ומושחין ממנו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is the oil vessel, named for the anointing done from it.

4:4.headline: Move the full jars, never the little jug
4:4.body: Elisha tells her to move each full jar aside. Rashi brings a midrash that the small jug must stay put: God made it like a spring, and a spring does not move.

sources.quote: לְפִי שֶׁהַקָּבָּ"ה עוֹשֵׂהוּ כְּמַעְיָן, וְאֵין דֶּרֶךְ מַעְיָן לְזוּזוֹ מִמְּקוֹמוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says she moved the full jars but not the oil jug, because God made it like a spring, and a spring does not move.

sources.quote: כי מעשה נס לא יהיה אלא במקום שהתחיל בו
sources.says: Radak says she was not to move, because a miracle happens only in the place where it began.

4:6.headline: The oil stopped, or the oil price stood high
4:6.body: Read plainly, the oil stopped flowing. A midrash reads ויעמד as the price of oil going up. Malbim says the oil stayed inside the jug, ready for later.

sources.quote: וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה: הוֹקִיר שַׁעַר הַשֶּׁמֶן
sources.says: Rashi says it stopped coming, and brings a midrash that the price of oil went up.

sources.quote: רק עמד בתוך האסוך
sources.says: Malbim says the oil did not run out but stood inside the jug, still able to give more later.

4:7.headline: Living on what is left, until the dead live again
4:7.body: Elisha says she and her sons will live on the rest of the money. The sages read 'the rest' as lasting a very long time: until the dead come back to life.

sources.quote: וְלִחְיוֹת אַתְּ וּבָנַיִךְ בַּנּוֹתָר, עַד שֶׁיִּחְיוּ הַמֵּתִים
sources.says: Rashi says there was enough for every debt, and for her and her sons to live on the rest until the dead are revived.

sources.quote: ואמרו חכמינו זכרונם לברכה תחיי בנותר עד שיחיו המתים
sources.says: Malbim cites the sages: 'you will live on the rest' until the dead live again.

4:8.headline: A 'great' woman: rich, known, or God-fearing
4:8.body: The verse calls her אשה גדולה, a great woman. Radak says she was wealthy and well known. The Targum says she feared sin.

sources.quote: חשובה בעלת נכסים ובעלת השם
sources.says: Radak says she was important, owned property and had a name, and notes the Targum calls her one who feared sin.

sources.quote: אִתְּתָא דַחֲלַת חֶטְאִין
sources.says: The Targum renders it 'a woman who feared sin'.

4:16.headline: Three readings of 'at this living time'
4:16.body: Rashi reads כעת חיה as 'just as you are alive now'. Radak reads חיה as a woman giving birth, as the sages use it. Ralbag says the present moment is the only time that is 'alive', because the past is gone and the future has not come.

sources.quote: כְּמוֹ שֶׁאַתְּ קַיֶּמֶת הַיּוֹם וּלְשָׁלוֹם
sources.says: Rashi says it means: as you are alive and well today, so you will be at this time, holding a son.

sources.quote: והיולדת תקרא חיה בדברי רז"ל
sources.says: Radak says it means the time she is ready to give birth, since the sages call a woman in labor חיה.

sources.quote: וקרא העת ההיא חיה להיות זה החלק מהזמן לבדו נמצא
sources.says: Ralbag says the present is called living because it is the only part of time that exists.

4:16.headline: Do not lie to me, or do not give what fails
4:16.body: כזב usually means a lie. The commentators read it like a spring 'whose waters do not fail': she asks not for a son who will be taken away.

sources.quote: אַל תַּרְאֵנִי דָּבָר שֶׁיִּפְסֹק
sources.says: Rashi says she means: do not show me something that will stop; give me only a son who will live.

sources.quote: ענינו דבר הנפסק
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means something that stops, as in waters that do not fail.

4:23.headline: Not a holiday, or not long since your last visit
4:23.body: Her husband says, 'It is not new moon or Sabbath.' The sages learn that people visited their teacher on those days. Radak's father reads it as: not even a month or a week has passed since you saw him.

sources.quote: למדו רז"ל מזה כי חייב אדם להקביל פני רבו בשבת וברגל
sources.says: Radak says the sages learn from here that a person should visit his teacher on Sabbath and festivals.

sources.quote: ואדוני אבי ז"ל פירש לא עבר לא חדש ולא שבת שראית אותו
sources.says: Radak brings his father's reading: no month or week has passed since you saw him, so why go now.

4:28.headline: Do not lead me into a mistake
4:28.body: תשלה is rare. Rashi and Radak read it as 'mislead', because the Aramaic word for an error is שלו. The Targum reads it as 'do not test me'.

sources.quote: ותשלה כמו תשגה תרגום שגגה שלו
sources.says: Radak says it means 'mislead', since the Aramaic for error is שלו, and brings the Targum's 'do not test me'.

sources.quote: לֹא תַשְׁגֶּה אוֹתִי עַל דְּבַר טָעוּת
sources.says: Rashi says it means: do not lead me astray with something false.

4:34.headline: Stretched out over the child, or bent with tiredness
4:34.body: ויגהר is rare. The Targum reads it as exhaustion. Menachem, cited by Rashi, reads it from the scene: Elisha stretched himself out over the boy.

sources.quote: פִּתְרוֹן הַמִּלָּה כְּפִי עִנְיָנָהּ, נִשְׁתַּטַּח עָלָיו
sources.says: Rashi notes the Targum reads it as tiredness, and Menachem explains from context that he stretched out on him.

sources.quote: ענין השתטחות הגוף
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means stretching the body out, as when Elijah bent down to the ground.

4:39.headline: A herb named for lighting up the eyes
4:39.body: ארת is a rare word for wild plants. A sage in the Talmud says it is arugula, called אורות, 'lights', because it brightens the eyes. Others read it simply as greens.

sources.quote: למה נקרא שמו אורות שמאירות את העינים
sources.says: Radak says it means greens, and brings Rabbi Yochanan: arugula is called אורות because it brightens the eyes.

sources.quote: גַּרְגִּיר שֶׁקּוֹרִין אוֹרְגָּא, שֶׁמֵּאִיר אֶת הָעֵינַיִם
sources.says: Rashi says it is arugula, which brightens the eyes, and some read it as greens.

4:42.headline: Fresh grain carried in its husk, or in a sack
4:42.body: בצקלנו appears only here. Following the Targum, Radak and Metzudat Zion read it as 'in its husk'. Ralbag reads it as the bag the man carried his gift in.

sources.quote: בקליפתו כתרגומו ופירוכן בלבושיה
sources.says: Radak says it means in its husk, following the Targum.

sources.quote: ר"ל בכלי שהיה לו לשאת בו אלו הדברים
sources.says: Ralbag says it means the container he had for carrying these things.

5:2.headline: נערה קטנה: a young girl, and from a town called Naaron
5:2.body: נערה and קטנה both seem to say she was young. Rashi and Radak, following the sages, say קטנה tells her age, and נערה hints at her town, Naaron.

sources.quote: רִיבָה קְטַנָּה, מֵעִיר נַעֲרוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says she was a little girl from the town of Naaron.

sources.quote: קרי לה נערה וקרי לה קטנה אלא קטנה היתה והיתה ממקום ששמו נערון
sources.says: Radak says the sages ask why she is called both נערה and קטנה, and answer that she was young and came from a place named Naaron.

5:3.headline: אחלי: "if only", from the word for pleading
5:3.body: אחלי is a rare word for a wish. Rashi and Metzudat Zion link it to ויחל משה, "Moses pleaded". Radak says it is shaped like אשרי, and the Targum renders it טובי, "how good it would be".

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן וַיְחַל משֶׁה, בַּקָּשׁוֹת כָּל הַמִּתְפַּלְּלִים עָלָיו יִהְיוּ
sources.says: Rashi says it is from "Moses pleaded": may the requests of all who pray for him come before the prophet.

sources.quote: ענין בקשה, כמו (שמות לב יא): ויחל משה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means a request, like "Moses pleaded" in Exodus 32:11.

sources.quote: ואחלי שם בפלס אשרי ותרגום יונתן טובי רבוני
sources.says: Radak says אחלי is a noun on the pattern of אשרי, and the Targum renders "how good for my master".

5:3.headline: Healing a leper is called "gathering" him back in
5:3.body: יאסף means "gather in". A leper had to live apart from others. Radak and Metzudat David say healing is called gathering because the healed man is brought back among people.

sources.quote: ונקראת רפואת הצרעת אסיפה מפני שהמצורע ישב בדד ובהרפאו יאסף בין בני אדם
sources.says: Radak says healing leprosy is called gathering because the leper sits alone, and when healed he is gathered back among people.

sources.quote: לפי שבעודו בצרעתו, מחוץ למחנה מושבו, וכאשר יתרפא, יאסף ויכנס אל המחנה
sources.says: Metzudat David says that while leprous he lives outside the camp, and when healed he is gathered back into it.

5:6.headline: "Gather him from his leprosy": two reasons for the word
5:6.body: Rashi says the healed leper is gathered back among people. Ralbag gives another reason: leprosy breaks the body apart, and healing gathers it back into one.

sources.quote: 'אֲסֵפָה' בִּמְצֹרָע הִיא לְשׁוֹן רְפוּאָתוֹ, כִּי בְּהִתְרַפּאוֹתוֹ הוּא נֶאֱסָף אֶל תּוֹךְ בְּנֵי אָדָם
sources.says: Rashi says gathering, for a leper, means healing, because when healed he is gathered back among people.

sources.quote: ונקרא הרפואה מהצרעת אסיפה כי הצרעת תעשה מהאחד רבים
sources.says: Ralbag says the cure is called gathering because leprosy makes one body into many pieces.

5:9.headline: Written "his horse", read aloud as "his horses"
5:9.body: The written word means one horse, but it is read aloud as many. Radak says the written form is Naaman on his own horse, and the read form is the men who came with him.

sources.quote: כן כתיב וקרי בסוסיו לשון רבים הכתוב אומר על עצמו שהיה הוא רוכב בסוסו והקרי הוא על הבאים עמו
sources.says: Radak says it is written singular and read plural: the written form is about Naaman riding his horse, the read form about those who came with him.

5:12.headline: "I could wash there and be clean", or "Am I clean?"
5:12.body: Naaman's words can be a boast: if washing heals, I could wash in Damascus's rivers. Radak and Ralbag also hear a bitter question: I wash in them all the time, and am I clean?

sources.quote: אם בטבילה אטהר ארחץ בהם ואטהר
sources.says: Radak says one reading is: if immersion makes me clean, I will wash in them and be clean.

sources.quote: בתמיה וכי אני טהור בעבור זה
sources.says: Radak says another reading is a question: am I clean because of this?

sources.quote: הלא אני רוחץ בהם תמיד האם טהרתי מצרעתי מפני רחיצתי בהם
sources.says: Ralbag says it means: I always wash in them, and have I been cleansed of my leprosy by it?

5:17.headline: Why Naaman asks for two mule-loads of earth
5:17.body: Rashi says Naaman wanted holy soil from the land of Israel, to carry home and build an altar from it. Radak says he asked instead of just taking it, so the altar would not be built from stolen earth.

sources.quote: מֵאֲדָמָה זוֹ מֵאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהִיא קְדוֹשָׁה
sources.says: Rashi says he wanted earth from the land of Israel, which is holy.

sources.quote: וְאֶשָּׂאֶנָּה לְעִירִי וְאֶעֱשֶׂה אוֹתָהּ מִזְבֵּחַ
sources.says: Rashi says Naaman meant to carry it to his city and make an altar of it.

sources.quote: אלא אמר שלא יעשה המזבח לה' בגזלה אם לא מרצון הנביא והמלך
sources.says: Radak says he asked so that the altar to God would not be made from stolen earth, but with the prophet's and king's consent.

5:18.headline: Naaman's bow in the idol's temple is forced on him
5:18.body: Naaman's king leans on his arm, so when the king bows, Naaman bends too. Rashi says he bows against his will. Malbim says he only bends so the king can bow, which is not real worship.

sources.quote: עַל כָּרְחִי, כְּשֶׁשּׁוֹחֶה אֲדוֹנִי וְהוּא נִשְׁעָן עַל יָדִי
sources.says: Rashi says he bows against his will, when his master bows while leaning on his hand.

sources.quote: כי הוא אינו משתחווה רק שוחה קומתו לצורך השתחויית המלך
sources.says: Malbim says he does not really bow, he only bends his body so the king can bow.

5:23.headline: הואל: "please agree", or "swear to me"?
5:23.body: הואל usually means "please, agree". Rashi, following the sages, reads it as "swear that Elisha sent you". Metzudat Zion keeps the plain sense, "be willing".

sources.quote: הוֹאֵל. הִשָּׁבַע שֶׁשְּׁלַחֲךָ
sources.says: Rashi says הואל means: swear that he sent you.

sources.quote: ולדעת חכמינו זכרונם לברכה השביעו
sources.says: Malbim says that in the sages' view Naaman made Gehazi swear.

sources.quote: רצה, כמו (לקמן ו ג): הואל נא ולך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means "be willing", as in II Kings 6:3.

5:23.headline: ויפרץ is ויפצר with two letters swapped
5:23.body: In verse 16 Naaman pressed Elisha to take a gift, ויפצר, and was refused. Here he presses Gehazi with the same word, letters swapped. Metzudat Zion says the two are one word.

sources.quote: ויפרוץ. הוא הפוך מן ויפצר, והיא היא
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says ויפרץ is ויפצר with letters reversed, and means the same.

sources.quote: נעמן הפציר בגחזי לקחת ככרים
sources.says: Metzudat David says Naaman urged Gehazi to take the talents of silver.

5:23.headline: חרטים: two cloths, or two long purses
5:23.body: חרטים is a rare word. Rashi gives Menachem's view, kinds of cloth, and another view, long purses. Metzudat Zion says purses, as in Isaiah 3:22.

sources.quote: מִינֵי בְּגָדִים וְסוּדָרִין
sources.says: Rashi says Menachem takes them as kinds of garments and cloths.

sources.quote: וְהַפּוֹתְרִין אוֹמְרִין: בִּשְׁנֵי חֲרִיטֵי, בִּשְׁנֵי כִּיסִין אֲרֻכִּים
sources.says: Rashi says other explainers say they were two long purses.

sources.quote: מין כיסים, וכן (שם ג כב): והמטפחות והחריטים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says they were a kind of purse, as in Isaiah 3:22.

5:24.headline: העפל: a high tower, or a hidden place?
5:24.body: עפל is a rare word. Radak and Ralbag say it is a high place with a strong house. The Targum calls it a hidden place, and Metzudat David links it to אופל, darkness, where no one would see.

sources.quote: מקום גבוה שבו היה בית כמו עופל ובחן
sources.says: Radak says it is a high place with a house on it.

sources.quote: ויונתן תרגם לאתר כסי תרגם אותו מן עפולים שפירושו תחתוניות שהוא מקום נסתר
sources.says: Radak says the Targum's "hidden place" reads it from a word for low parts, a hidden spot.

sources.quote: הנה העופל הוא מקום גבוהה והיה שם בית חזק
sources.says: Ralbag says the Ophel is a high place with a strong house.

sources.quote: או, כמו האופל באל״ף ורוצה לומר: למקום חושך, לבל יראה מי
sources.says: Metzudat David says it may be like אופל, darkness: a dark place, so no one would see.

5:24.headline: ויפקד: he counted the silver, stored it, or appointed buyers
5:24.body: פקד has many senses. Ralbag offers three: Gehazi counted the coins, left them in safekeeping, or put men in charge of buying with them. Radak says he stored them there to hide them from Elisha.

sources.quote: אחשוב שהרצון בזה שכבר מנה בהיותו בבית סך המטבע
sources.says: Ralbag first suggests that in the house he counted the sum of the coins.

sources.quote: או יהיה מענין פקדון ואם הוא מהקל והרצון בו שהפקידו בביתו או יהיה מענין פקידות
sources.says: Ralbag adds that it may mean he deposited it in his house, or that he appointed people.

sources.quote: הפקיד הכסף והבגדים שם שרצה להעלים מאלישע
sources.says: Radak says he deposited the silver and clothes there because he wanted to hide them from Elisha.

5:26.headline: "Did my heart not go with you?": Elisha's mind was there
5:26.body: Maimonides says לב can mean thought. Elisha means: in my mind I was there when it happened. Radak agrees, and the Targum says it was shown to Elisha by prophecy.

sources.quote: הוא גם שמה של המחשבה
sources.says: Maimonides says לב is also a name for thought.

sources.quote: כלומר הייתי נוכח במחשבתי כאשר אירע כך וכך
sources.says: Maimonides says Elisha's words mean: I was present in my thought when this happened.

sources.quote: כי לבי ומחשבתי היה עמך בלכתך
sources.says: Radak says Elisha's heart and thought were with Gehazi as he went.

sources.quote: בְּרוּחַ נְבוּאָה אִתְחַוָא לִי
sources.says: The Targum renders it "by the spirit of prophecy it was shown to me".

5:27.headline: "And Naaman's leprosy": the silver is yours, and the disease too
5:27.body: The verse opens with "and", as if words are missing. Metzudat David and Radak fill them in: the silver is given to you, and Naaman's leprosy with it.

sources.quote: יחסר ראשית הדברים, וכאומר, הכסף נתון לך, וגם הצרעת
sources.says: Metzudat David says the start of the sentence is missing: the silver is given to you, and the leprosy too.

sources.quote: ופירושו הכסף נתון לך והצרעת
sources.says: Radak says it means the silver is given to you, and the leprosy.

6:6.headline: Did the iron float, or did Elisha make it float?
6:6.body: ויצף can mean the iron floated up by itself. It can also mean someone made it float, so Elisha is the one who raised it.

sources.quote: ויצף. פועל עומד אשר הציף את מי ים סוף פועל יוצא ויש לפרש ויצף פועל יוצא כלומר הנביא הציפו
sources.says: Radak reads the verb as 'it floated', and also allows 'he made it float', meaning the prophet floated it.

6:8.headline: The 'so-and-so place' is a hidden place
6:8.body: פלני, our 'so-and-so', is read as 'covered'. The king of Aram names a hidden spot for his camp so Israel will not find it.

sources.quote: פְּלוֹנִי, לְשׁוֹן: כִּי יִפָּלֵא 'יִתְכַּסֵּי'
sources.says: Rashi links the word to יפלא, 'it is hidden', and says it means covered.

sources.quote: לַאֲתַר כַּסִי טְמִיר
sources.says: The Aramaic translation renders it 'to a covered, hidden place'.

6:8.headline: A place too secret to be spoken of
6:8.body: אלמני is tied to אלם, 'mute': a place no one names out loud. Ralbag adds it may also be עלמוני, 'hidden'.

sources.quote: אלמוני. מלשון אלם, כי לא ידובר בו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word comes from 'mute', because the place is not spoken about.

sources.quote: כי אל"ף אלמוני בזה המקו' ישמש במקו' עי"ן כמו עלמוני והוא ענין נעלם
sources.says: Ralbag suggests the aleph stands in for an ayin, making it 'hidden'.

sources.quote: אַלְמוֹנִי. מִבְּלִי שֵׁם
sources.says: Rashi says it means without a name.

6:9.headline: The Arameans have gone down to hide
6:9.body: נחתים, found only here, is read as 'going down', as in the Aramaic word for descending. The soldiers camped in a low spot so no one would see them.

sources.quote: נחתים. מן הנחת ה' גבוריך ותרגום וירד ונחת ופי' יורדים וחונים שם ואמר נחתים כי במקום מורד חנו להסתר שם
sources.says: Radak says the word means going down and camping, because they camped in a low place to hide.

sources.quote: והרצון בו שהם עומדים שם בנחת בדרך שיעלם היותם שם
sources.says: Ralbag offers another reading: from נחת, 'quiet', meaning they wait there quietly so no one knows.

6:23.headline: 'No more raids' meant for that time, not forever
6:23.body: The very next verse has Aram attacking again. Radak says עוד here means 'any more at that time', not 'ever again'.

sources.quote: אינו אומר עוד לעולם שהרי אומר ויהי אחרי כן ויקבוץ בן הדד אלא פירוש עוד באותו הזמן
sources.says: Radak says the word does not mean forever, since Ben-Hadad attacks right after, but only during that time.

6:25.headline: The written word is crude; the read word is polite
6:25.body: The text is written חרי יונים, plainly 'dove dung'. Readers say דביונים instead, a cleaner way to say the same thing.

sources.quote: חריונים. כן כתיב וקרי דביונים ופי' צואת יונים והכתוב אומר מה שיוצא מחור היונים והקרי לשון נקיה יותר מה שזב מן היונים
sources.says: Radak says the written form means what comes out of the dove, and the read form is a cleaner word for it.

6:32.headline: 'Son of the murderer' points back to Ahab and Naboth
6:32.body: Elisha calls the king בן המרצח, 'son of the murderer'. The commentators say this means Ahab, who had Naboth killed, and now his son wants to kill again.

sources.quote: בן המרצח. בן אחאב שרצח נבות כן הוא רוצה לרצחני
sources.says: Radak says it means the son of Ahab, who murdered Naboth; the son now wants to murder Elisha.

sources.quote: בן המרצח. את אחאב קורא מרצח
sources.says: Metzudat David says Elisha calls Ahab a murderer because he agreed to Jezebel's killing of the prophets.

6:33.headline: Why should I hope, or why should I pray?
6:33.body: אוחיל usually means 'wait in hope'. The Aramaic translation reads it as 'pray', and Ralbag also links it to a word for pain.

sources.quote: ויונתן תרגם מה אצלי תרגם אוחיל כמו אחלה
sources.says: Radak reads it as 'what more can I hope for', and notes the Targum translated it 'pray', like אחלה.

sources.quote: והוא מענין מעי מעי אוחילה
sources.says: Ralbag offers a reading tied to 'my insides, I writhe', from pain.

7:2.headline: Windows in the sky: for rain, or for grain falling like manna?
7:2.body: The officer mocks: even if God made windows in heaven. Radak says he meant windows to let rain fall, or, as an overstatement, to drop wheat and barley the way the manna came down.

sources.quote: להמטיר או בדרך הפלגה להוריד חטים ושעורים על דרך ירידת המן
sources.says: Radak says the windows are either for rain or, as an overstatement, to send down wheat and barley like the manna.

sources.quote: אִילוּ יְיָ פְּתַח כַּוִין וּמָחִית טוּבָא מִן שְׁמַיָא
sources.says: Targum Jonathan renders it 'if God opened windows and brought down plenty from heaven'.

7:4.headline: 'We will die' three times: they have nothing left to lose
7:4.body: The lepers say 'we will die' three times: in the city, at the gate, or at the enemy camp. Malbim says that is the point: death is certain here, so going to the Arameans can only gain them life.

sources.quote: ואם ימיתנו לא נפסיד מאומה שבל"ז ומתנו ועל זה אמר ג"פ ומתנו
sources.says: Malbim says that if the Arameans kill them they lose nothing, since they will die anyway, and that is why 'we will die' is said three times.

sources.quote: כאומר מה בכך אם נמות, הלא ממה נפשך אנו מעותדים למיתה
sources.says: The Metzudat David says they meant: so what if we die, we are bound to die either way.

7:9.headline: 'Guilt will find us': the king's punishment, or a real sin?
7:9.body: Rashi and Ralbag read עון here as punishment: the king will hold the lepers guilty for keeping quiet. Malbim reads it as true sin, because starving people's lives hang on the news.

sources.quote: מִתְחַיְּבִין אָנוּ לַמַּלְכוּת
sources.says: Rashi says it means they will be held liable by the king.

sources.quote: וימצאנו עונש על אשר לא בשרנו הבשורה הזאת
sources.says: Ralbag says punishment will find them for not bringing the good news.

sources.quote: וימצאו עון שבתוך כך יש פקוח נפשות העטופים ברעב
sources.says: Malbim says waiting would be a sin because the lives of the starving are at stake.

9:1.headline: A flask, not a horn, hints that Jehu's line will not last
9:1.body: Jehu is anointed from a פך, a small flask. Radak brings the sages' teaching that kings anointed from a flask, Saul and Jehu, did not found lasting lines, while David and Solomon, anointed from a horn, did.

sources.quote: ואמרו שאול ויהוא נמשחו בפך לא נמשכה מלכותן דוד ושלמה שנמשחו בקרן נמשכה מלכותן
sources.says: Radak cites the sages: Saul and Jehu were anointed from a flask and their rule did not last, while David and Solomon were anointed from a horn and theirs did.

sources.quote: שם כלי מיוחד לשמן
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says פך is the name of a vessel made for oil.

9:4.headline: Who is 'the prophet': the young man, or his teacher Elisha?
9:4.body: The verse says הנער הנער הנביא, "the young man, the young man the prophet." Rashi and the Targum read "the prophet's young man," a student of Elisha, while Malbim reads a young man who was a prophet himself, which is why he added words Elisha never gave him.

sources.quote: נַעֲרוֹ שֶל אֱלִישָׁע הַנָּבִיא
sources.says: Rashi says it means the young man of Elisha the prophet, following the Targum.

sources.quote: עִלֵימָא תַּלְמִידָא דִנְבִיָא
sources.says: The Targum renders it "the young man, the student of the prophet."

sources.quote: מצד שהוא הנער הנביא שהוא נביא בעצמו
sources.says: Malbim says he went as a prophet in his own right, and that is why he added to Elisha's message.

9:11.headline: Why the officers call the prophet a madman
9:11.body: Jehu's men call the prophet המשגע, "this madman." The commentators say a prophet deep in prophecy could look like a madman, cut off from the world, and Radak adds that men loyal to Baal used the word to mock him.

sources.quote: היו קוראים לנביא משוגע לפי שפעמים בעת הנבואה היה מנהגם כמו המשוגע
sources.says: Radak says they called a prophet mad because in prophecy prophets sometimes behaved like madmen.

sources.quote: היו קוראים לנביא ה' משוגע דרך בזיון
sources.says: Radak adds that the wicked of Israel, whose hearts were with Baal, called God's prophet mad as an insult.

sources.quote: לפי שבעת שהיה מתבודד בנבואה, היה נדמה להם כמשתגע
sources.says: Metzudat David says that when the prophet withdrew into prophecy he seemed to them like a madman.

9:13.headline: The 'bone' of the stairs: the very steps, or a sundial?
9:13.body: גרם usually means bone. Metzudat Zion says it means "the very" stairs, the way עצם, bone, also means "the very" day, while Rashi and the Targum read it as stairs built to tell the hours by the shadow.

sources.quote: עצם וגרם, אחד הוא
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says גרם and עצם, bone, are the same, and both can mean the thing itself.

sources.quote: כְּמִין מַעֲלוֹת עֲשׂוּיוֹת לְמוּל שְׁעוֹת הַיּוֹם
sources.says: Rashi says these were steps made to match the hours of the day, with the shadow dropping one step each hour.

sources.quote: לִדְרַג שַׁעֲיָא
sources.says: The Targum renders it "the steps of the hours."

sources.quote: אל המעלה העליונה שבמעלות
sources.says: Radak says it means the top step of the stairs.

9:24.headline: Shot between the arms he stretched out to take interest
9:24.body: Jehu's arrow hits Jehoram בין זרעיו, "between his arms." Rashi brings a midrash that Jehoram had lent at interest to the man who fed the prophets, so he was struck between the arms he reached out to collect it.

sources.quote: לְכָךְ נֶאֱמַר: וַיַּךְ אֶת יְהוֹרָם בֵּין זְרוֹעָיו, שֶׁפָּשְׁטוּ לִטֹּל רִבִּית
sources.says: Rashi, citing Midrash Tanchuma, says Jehoram lent at interest to the man who fed the prophets, and so he was hit between the arms that reached out to take the interest.

9:26.headline: Naboth's sons: killed with him, never born, or robbed?
9:26.body: The story of Naboth in I Kings 21 never mentions his sons. Radak gives three readings: they were killed with him, they are the children he would have had, or, as his father taught, they are the heirs whose land was stolen.

sources.quote: יש שאומרים בניו נהרגו עמו ומהם אמרו בנים העתידים לצאת ממנו
sources.says: Radak says the sages disagree: some say his sons were killed with him, others that it means the sons he would have had.

sources.quote: ואת דמי בניו שגזל מהם נחלתם
sources.says: Radak's father explained it as the sons whose inheritance Ahab stole.

sources.quote: אמר דמי בניו העתידים לצאת ממנו
sources.says: Ralbag takes it as the sons who would have been born to him.

9:31.headline: Jezebel calls Jehu 'Zimri,' the name of an earlier king-killer
9:31.body: Zimri had killed his master, King Elah. Rashi and Metzudat David hear her offering peace, as if this were nothing new, while Malbim hears a warning: Zimri was killed, and Israel would not crown a man who murdered his master.

sources.quote: אִם הָרַגְתָּ אֶת אֲדוֹנְךָ אֵין זֶה דָּבָר חָדָשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says she meant: if you killed your master, that is nothing new, since Zimri also killed Elah son of Baasha.

sources.quote: וכאילו באה להקל אשמתו, לומר שכבר היה לעולמים, וכדי להחניפו אמרה כן
sources.says: Metzudat David says she tried to make his guilt seem small, as something that had happened before, to flatter him.

sources.quote: להזכיר כי זמרי נהרג ולא אבו ישראל להמליך את המורד והורג אדוניו
sources.says: Malbim says she named Zimri to remind them that Zimri was killed and Israel refused to crown a rebel who killed his master.

9:33.headline: Thrown from the window, as she had Naboth stoned
9:33.body: The word is written שמטהו, "throw him down," but read שמטוה, "throw her down." Radak says the written form hints at Naboth, whom she had stoned, and Ralbag says her fall was itself a stoning, measure for measure.

sources.quote: והכתיב יש בו דרש רמז לנבות שצותה לשמוט אותו ולסקלו
sources.says: Radak says the written spelling hints at Naboth: she ordered him thrown down and stoned, so Jehu ordered her thrown down.

sources.quote: וזהו סקילה כמו שסוקל נבות
sources.says: Ralbag says throwing her down was a form of stoning, just as Naboth was stoned, measure for measure.

9:35.headline: Why the dogs left her skull, feet and palms
9:35.body: Only Jezebel's skull, feet and palms were found. Rashi and Radak bring the sages' teaching that she used to dance before brides and grooms with her hands and feet and sway her head, so these parts were spared.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָיְתָה מְרַקֶּדֶת לִפְנֵי חֲתָנִים בְּיָדֶיהָ וּבְרַגְלֶיהָ וּמְכַשְׁכֶּשֶׁת בְּרֹאשָׁהּ
sources.says: Rashi cites the sages: she would dance before grooms with her hands and feet and shake her head.

sources.quote: לזכות שהיתה מרקדת לפני הכלות נשארו בה הרגלים
sources.says: Radak brings the midrash that her feet, palms and skull were left because she danced, clapped and swayed her head before brides.

sources.quote: בזכות שהיתה מרקדת ברגליה, ומטפחת בידיה, ומרכנת בראשה, לפני הכלה לשמחה
sources.says: Metzudat David, citing Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer, says the dogs did not eat these parts because she danced, clapped and nodded her head to bring joy to a bride.
